nodes.name: Icehouse Ventures
nodes.subtitle: NZ's most active VC, backing Kiwi founders building globally transformative companies.
nodes.location: Auckland, New Zealand (Parnell — Textile Centre, 125 St Georges Bay Rd)

metadata.bio: Icehouse Ventures is an Auckland-based venture capital firm and one of New Zealand's most active early-stage investors. It traces its origins to 2003, when the Ice Angels angel network was formed within The Icehouse, the entrepreneurship incubator founded in 2001 as a joint venture between the University of Auckland and private partners. The angel network raised its first fund in 2013 and was formally consolidated and rebranded as Icehouse Ventures in 2019, when external shareholders including Simplicity KiwiSaver, Jarden, and Sir Stephen Tindall's K1W1 came on board. Since 2003 it has invested over NZ$800 million into 390+ Kiwi-founded companies, and operates funds and networks including Ice Angels, Arc Angels, and the student-led Firstcut Ventures.
metadata.founded: 2003 (Ice Angels network); consolidated and rebranded as Icehouse Ventures in 2019. Parent The Icehouse founded 2001.
metadata.investmentStage: Pre-seed to pre-IPO (incubation, seed, early stage, and growth)
metadata.sectorFocus: Technology and innovation; sector-agnostic across software, deep tech, agritech, climate/sustainable tech, biotech, and consumer, plus a female-founder focused fund.

nodes.name: Sharesies
nodes.subtitle: NZ wealth platform giving anyone with $5 the same investing access as someone with $5m

metadata.bio: Sharesies is a New Zealand wealth-development (fintech) platform that lets people invest small amounts in shares, ETFs, KiwiSaver and other products, including fractional shares. Founded in Wellington in 2017, it operates across New Zealand and Australia. By 2025/2026 the company reported around 930,000 to over 1,000,000 investors and more than NZ$12 billion in wealth managed on the platform. It is led by a three co-CEO ("3EO") structure made up of co-founders Brooke Roberts, Leighton Roberts and Sonya Williams.
metadata.statusDetail: Active and independent; valued at ~NZ$500m at its October 2021 Series C, with ~930,000-1M+ investors and NZ$12B+ in wealth managed reported by 2025/2026.
metadata.fundingNotable: Raised NZ$25m in Dec 2020 (Trade Me, Icehouse Ventures, K1W1/Stephen Tindall) and a ~NZ$50m (A$48m) Series C in Oct 2021 led by US VC Amplo with Icehouse Ventures and others, valuing the company at ~NZ$500m.
metadata.verifyNote: All major facts independently verified via fresh searches. Founders, the 3EO co-CEO structure, 2017 Wellington founding, active/independent status, ~NZ$500m Oct 2021 Series C (led by Amplo, with Icehouse Ventures) and the Dec 2020 NZ$25m round (Trade Me, Icehouse Ventures, K1W1) all confirmed. Icehouse backing confirmed on icehouseventures.co.nz (backed founders at the 2018 Showcase, plus the later rounds). The draft's "1M+ investors / NZ$12B+ assets by 2025" claim is supported by current 2025/2026 reporting (~930,000-1M+ investors, NZ$12B+ wealth); some 2024 sources (Wikipedia/Icehouse page) still cite the stale 700K-800K / NZ$5B figures, so the description was softened to a range. Minor refinements: Richard Clark recast as Co-founder & CTO, and founder bios tightened where prior education claims (e.g., a specific Brooke Roberts Stanford credential) could not be independently confirmed and were generalised. Confidence remains high.
metadata.notes: Six co-founders total (Brooke Roberts, Leighton Roberts, Sonya Williams, Richard Clark, Ben Crotty, Martyn Smith), all confirmed by Wikipedia and the Icehouse Ventures portfolio page. Only three (the two Robertses and Williams) are active executive leaders under the "3EO" co-CEO model; Richard Clark is the technology lead (CTO). LinkedIn URLs confirmed for the three co-CEOs; not found/confirmed for Clark, Crotty and Smith (left null). This is the Wellington, NZ fintech, distinct from any same-named foreign entity. Brooke and Leighton Roberts are married. ~NZ$500m valuation is as of the Oct 2021 Series C; no newer public valuation confirmed.

nodes.name: Vessev
nodes.subtitle: Auckland maker of certified electric hydrofoiling passenger vessels

metadata.bio: Vessev is a New Zealand company that designs and builds electric hydrofoiling vessels and propulsion technology, lifting boats above the water to cut energy consumption by up to ~90%. Its flagship VS-9 launched in 2024 as what the company calls the world's first certified electric hydrofoiling vessel for commercial tourism, entering passenger service with Auckland ferry operator Fullers360 in January 2025. The company is expanding internationally (US office, a Northern Ireland resort customer) and is developing a larger VS-18 commuter ferry. It is headquartered in Auckland and backed by NZ and offshore venture investors.
metadata.statusDetail: Active and scaling; VS-9 ("Kermadec") in commercial passenger service with Fullers360 (Auckland) since Jan 2025, US office opened 2025, first European customer (Finn Lough resort, Northern Ireland), VS-18 commuter ferry in development.
metadata.fundingNotable: Backed by Icehouse Ventures (early/seed investor via Seed Fund II and largest shareholder, reported ~27% stake added to via its Growth Fund II), Blackbird Ventures, K1W1 (Sir Stephen Tindall), Shasta Ventures, GD1, and US-based Field Family Investments, plus a small Port of Auckland stake; also received ~NZ$1.2m in EECA Low Emission Transport Fund grants across three grants. PitchBook lists ~US$3.62m total disclosed; full round amounts not publicly confirmed.
metadata.verifyNote: Independently confirmed via fresh searches: both founders (Max Olson — founder/original CEO, now CTO; Eric Laakmann — CEO, ex-Apple Watch, joined ~2020) verified across NZ Herald, Icehouse Ventures, Vessev and multiple outlets. Icehouse backing confirmed by its own portfolio page (Seed Fund II) and NZ Herald (~27% largest stake, Growth Fund II). Active status, VS-9/Fullers360 service, and investor list all confirmed. Corrections: softened the "co-founded Halter" claim (sources describe Olson as Halter's first CTO; Craig Piggott is founder/CEO); added Max Olson's LinkedIn URL surfaced in search; tightened oneLiner under 110 chars and removed the unverified Australia/Europe expansion phrasing from description/status (only US office and Northern Ireland customer are clearly sourced). Founding year remains ambiguous (2017/2018/2019); 2018 retained per Icehouse.
metadata.notes: Auckland NZ electric-hydrofoil maritime company (vessev.com) — not to be confused with same-named foreign entities. Founding year is ambiguous across sources: Icehouse states 2018, some press credits Max Olson with starting work in 2017, and Blackbird's page indicates 2019; 2018 retained as Icehouse's stated figure. Eric Laakmann (CEO) joined ~2020, not a day-one founder — Max Olson is the original founder/CEO, now CTO. Olson's exact founding role at Halter is described variously (co-founder vs. first CTO; Craig Piggott is Halter's founder/CEO), so bio wording softened.

nodes.name: Halter
nodes.subtitle: Solar smart collars and software to virtually fence, remotely move and monitor cattle from a phone

metadata.bio: Halter is a New Zealand agritech company that makes solar-powered, GPS-enabled smart collars plus farm-management software that let farmers virtually fence, remotely shift and proactively monitor cattle, using audio cues and vibration. Founded in 2016 by Craig Piggott (with co-founder Max Olson), it is headquartered in Auckland and has expanded into Australia and the United States, with an office in Boulder, Colorado. It reached unicorn status in 2025 with a NZ$1.65 billion (about US$1B) Series D. In March 2026 it raised a NZ$377 million (US$220M) Series E led by Founders Fund at a NZ$3.43 billion (US$2B) valuation, reporting roughly one million collars sold across 2,000+ farms and ranches.
metadata.statusDetail: Active and scaling internationally; unicorn since 2025. Operates in New Zealand, Australia and the US (offices in Auckland and Boulder, Colorado), with planned expansion into the UK, Ireland and South America.
metadata.fundingNotable: Raised NZ$377M (~US$220M) Series E in March 2026 at a NZ$3.43B (~US$2B) valuation, led by Founders Fund; reached unicorn status in 2025 with a NZ$1.65B (~US$1B) Series D (US$100M / NZ$165M). Investors include Founders Fund, Blackbird, BOND, Bessemer Venture Partners, DCVC, NewView Capital, Promus Ventures, Ubiquity, and Icehouse Ventures (first backed Craig Piggott via Seed Fund I in 2016).
metadata.verifyNote: Draft was substantially accurate. Independently confirmed: both founders (Piggott CEO, Olson first CTO, since left for Vessev) via Icehouse's portfolio page and Vessev/Blackbird sources; active status and 2025 unicorn milestone; Icehouse Ventures backing (Seed Fund I, 2016, ~200x return, ongoing investor); and the March 2026 Series E (NZ$377M/US$220M led by Founders Fund at NZ$3.43B/US$2B) via Halter's own release. Minor cleanups: shortened the oneLiner and trimmed the description; clarified the office as Boulder, Colorado; removed the unverifiable "Generate" from the named Series E investor list and the unsourced specific Series D LinkedIn/Vessev founding year. One discrepancy noted: NZ Herald headlines say "NZ$3.3B" while the company release and Caproasia say NZ$3.43B — kept the company figure.
metadata.notes: This is the NZ agritech Halter (halterhq.com), distinct from same-named foreign companies. Icehouse Ventures' own portfolio page names BOTH Craig Piggott and Max Olson as founders and states it first backed Piggott at 22 in 2016 via Seed Fund I — independently confirming both the co-founder claim and Icehouse backing. Max Olson left Halter and is now co-founder/CTO of Vessev. Valuation is reported in both NZD and USD; the company's own Series E release states NZ$3.43B / US$2B, though some NZ Herald headlines round to "NZ$3.3 billion." Series D figures cited as US$100M / NZ$165M at ~NZ$1.65B (Wikipedia/Icehouse). Wikipedia does not name investors but does not contradict Icehouse backing.

nodes.name: Tracksuit
nodes.subtitle: Always-on, affordable brand-tracking SaaS giving marketers real-time consumer insight

metadata.bio: Tracksuit is a New Zealand-founded SaaS company that provides always-on, affordable brand-tracking software, giving marketers real-time data on brand awareness, consideration, usage and perception through an AI-powered dashboard. It was built to make enterprise-grade brand tracking far cheaper than traditional studies (roughly NZ$20,000 versus NZ$100,000+). As of mid-2025 it serves 1,000+ customers and tracks around 10,000 brands across markets including New Zealand, Australia, the US, UK and Europe, with about 150 staff. It is widely cited as one of New Zealand's fastest-growing startups.
metadata.statusDetail: Active and scaling internationally; raised a US$25m (NZ$42m) Series B in June 2025 led by VMG Partners, bringing total raised to over US$70m / NZ$70m+ across three rounds.
metadata.fundingNotable: Raised NZ$70m+ across three rounds. Seed (2023): NZ$7.5m. Series A (Feb 2024): NZ$22m (reported as US$13.5m) at ~NZ$150m valuation, with Altos Ventures and Footwork joining alongside existing backers Blackbird and Icehouse Ventures. Series B (June 2025): US$25m / NZ$42m led by VMG Partners, with Blackbird, Icehouse Ventures, Altos Ventures and Footwork. Notable angels include Mark Ritson and Emily Kramer.
metadata.verifyNote: Founders (Connor Archbold, Matthew Herbert), both as Co-founder & Co-CEO, are independently confirmed (RNZ, EY, Blackbird, Icehouse). Icehouse Ventures backing confirmed directly from its own portfolio page (Seed Fund III "one of our earliest investments"). 2021 founding, Auckland HQ, Series B (US$25m/NZ$42m, June 2025, led by VMG Partners), and ~150 staff / 1,000+ customers / ~10,000 brands all confirmed. Changes: removed the unsourced claim that Herbert is based in London (Tracksuit has a UK office and Archbold is confirmed NZ-based, but I could not source Herbert's specific location, so set to null); softened the Series A funding line because sources report it as both NZ$22m and US$13.5m and some name Altos/Footwork (not VMG) as the Series A lead; trimmed the description's "Disney/Bondi Sands/Sharesies" and overly precise staff/geography claims to the parts I could verify. Confidence remains high.
metadata.notes: Distinct from same-named apparel/clothing brands; this is the NZ-founded brand-tracking SaaS (gotracksuit.com). Icehouse Ventures backing is confirmed: its own portfolio page calls Tracksuit "one of our earliest investments" via Seed Fund III and names it as a participating investor in both later rounds. Both founders are described as Co-CEOs by RNZ and EY. Series A figures vary by source/currency (NZ$22m vs US$13.5m), and some reports name Altos/Footwork as the lead while the Series B was clearly led by VMG Partners.

nodes.name: Crimson Education
nodes.subtitle: NZ edtech unicorn: university admissions consulting, tutoring and an online high school

metadata.bio: Crimson Education is an Auckland-founded edtech company providing personalised university admissions consulting, tutoring and college-prep services to help students gain entry to top global universities such as the Ivy League and Oxbridge. It also operates Crimson Global Academy, an online high school. The company operates across roughly 20-25 markets worldwide. In November 2024 it reached unicorn status at a NZ$1 billion-plus valuation following its Series D round, and remains active and privately held.
metadata.statusDetail: Active and privately held; reached unicorn status (NZ$1 billion-plus valuation) at its Series D in November 2024. Leadership has publicly discussed a potential future IPO but none has occurred.

nodes.name: Dawn Aerospace
nodes.subtitle: Space transportation company building reusable spaceplanes and green satellite propulsion systems.

metadata.bio: Dawn Aerospace is a space transportation company founded in 2017 that develops flight-proven green chemical satellite propulsion systems and a reusable, runway-launched suborbital spaceplane (the Mk-II Aurora). Its propulsion technology has flown on hundreds of thrusters in orbit, and on 12 November 2024 its Aurora spaceplane broke the sound barrier (Mach 1.1, ~82,000 ft), becoming the first New Zealand-designed and -manufactured aircraft to do so. The company runs a dual-headquarter model in Christchurch (NZ) and Delft (Netherlands) with operations across four countries and 120+ employees.
metadata.statusDetail: Operationally active; broke the sound barrier (Mach 1.1) with its Mk-II Aurora spaceplane in Nov 2024; 207+ thrusters deployed in space and 60+ spaceplane flights completed.
metadata.fundingNotable: Raised a US$20M Series A in Dec 2022 from Icehouse Ventures, GD1 and Movac at a ~$170M valuation; $42M+ total funding. Icehouse first backed the team in a ~$3.5M seed round in 2018.
metadata.verifyNote: Independently confirmed via Dawn's own About page, Icehouse Ventures' portfolio page, Wikipedia, and NZ business media. All five founders (Stefan Powell, Jeroen Wink, James Powell, Robert Werner, Tobias Knop) and their roles are correct; both Dawn and Icehouse list the identical five-person founding team. Icehouse backing confirmed (2018 seed + 2022 Series A co-investment). Status, US$20M Dec-2022 Series A at ~$170M valuation, $42M+ total funding, dual HQ, and the Nov 2024 Mach 1.1 milestone all verified. Minor refinements only: clarified Stefan also holds CTO title and noted the sound-barrier flight made Dawn the first NZ-designed AND -manufactured aircraft to go supersonic; confirmed Stefan's Rocket Lab/Hyperion background via The Org/Crunchbase. The draft was accurate.

Headquarters is dual-sited (Christchurch NZ + Delft NL) with additional offices in France and the US. This is the NZ/Netherlands spaceplane and satellite-propulsion company founded by Stefan and James Powell — distinct from any same-named foreign entity. All five founders are independently confirmed by both Dawn's About page and IV's portfolio page. Stefan Powell holds CEO and CTO titles. Employee count cited as 120+ (Wikipedia, Aug 2025) to 130+ (company site). LinkedIn URLs for co-founders other than Stefan Powell were not confirmed, so left null.

nodes.name: OpenStar Technologies
nodes.subtitle: NZ fusion startup pursuing power-positive electricity via levitated dipole reactors

metadata.bio: OpenStar Technologies is a Wellington (Lower Hutt), New Zealand fusion energy startup developing nuclear fusion reactors based on the levitated dipole concept, using high-temperature superconducting magnets to confine plasma. Founded in 2021 by Dr Ratu Mataira out of Victoria University of Wellington's Robinson Research Institute, it aims to deliver power-positive devices to the grid by the early 2030s. In October 2024 it created and confined plasma in its Marsden Class device, holding plasma at roughly 300,000C for 20 seconds. The Maori-led company is backed by Icehouse Ventures among other investors and is building a facility for its next device, Tahi.
metadata.statusDetail: Active and scaling. Achieved first plasma in its Marsden Class device on 31 Oct 2024 (300,000C for 20 seconds); in Feb 2026 levitated a half-tonne superconducting magnet and was announced for a NZ$35M loan from the NZ Government's Regional Infrastructure Fund to build a facility for its next device, Tahi. Reported ~55 staff as of mid-2025.
metadata.fundingNotable: NZ$10M (~US$6.2M) seed round (announced Aug 2023) led by Outset Ventures, with Icehouse Ventures, Blackbird, Radar, Ngai Tahu Holdings, K1W1 and Aspire; ~NZ$20M reported raised by 2024. Separately, a NZ$35M NZ Government loan via the Regional Infrastructure Fund announced Feb 2026 (debt, not equity).
metadata.verifyNote: Both founders confirmed via the official team page (openstar.tech/team): Ratu Mataira (Founder & CEO) and Thomas Berry (Co-founder & Chief Product Officer) — Berry is named only on the company site, not Wikipedia/Icehouse, but is independently sourced so retained. Icehouse backing confirmed (Icehouse portfolio page + blog). Status confirmed active. Corrected the government-fund name from "Regional Development Fund" to "Regional Infrastructure Fund" (RNZ/BusinessDesk/NBR/growregions.govt.nz) and clarified it is a loan; added Radar and Aspire to the seed investor list and a Feb 2026 half-tonne magnet levitation milestone. Description tightened for accuracy (early 2030s grid goal per Icehouse).
metadata.notes: Icehouse Ventures backing confirmed by Icehouse's own portfolio page and blog ("one of Icehouse Venture's latest investments") and corroborated by NBR/Outset listing it among seed participants. Seed-round headline figure is NZ$10M / US$6.2M led by Outset Ventures (Aug 2023); cumulative ~NZ$20M by 2024 per Wikipedia. The NZ$35M (Feb 2026) is a government LOAN via the Regional Infrastructure Fund, not equity. Ratu Mataira's LinkedIn verified; Thomas Berry's LinkedIn not located. Do not confuse with unrelated foreign entities sharing the "Openstar" name.

nodes.name: AskNicely
nodes.subtitle: Customer experience platform helping frontline service teams act on real-time NPS feedback.
nodes.location: Portland, USA (dual HQ with Auckland, New Zealand)

metadata.bio: AskNicely is a customer experience (CX) software company founded in 2014 in Auckland, New Zealand, that helps service businesses collect real-time customer feedback (built around the Net Promoter Score framework) and coach their frontline teams to act on it. The company began in an Auckland garden shed and now operates dual headquarters in Portland, Oregon and Auckland, with an additional office in the Netherlands. It serves more than 1,300 service brands worldwide. AskNicely raised a US$32M Series B led by Five Elms Capital in January 2022, bringing total disclosed funding to roughly US$47M.
metadata.statusDetail: Active and operating. Series B (US$32M, led by Five Elms Capital, January 2022). Aaron Ward stepped from CEO to Co-founder & Chief Strategy Officer in 2023 when Kirsten Newbold-Knipp was appointed CEO.
metadata.fundingNotable: ~US$47.2M total raised across 5 rounds (Crunchbase). Icehouse Ventures is an investor (listed on its official portfolio) but did not lead the named A/B rounds.

It was founded in New Zealand in 2021 by ex-Bell Gully corporate lawyer Min-Kyu Jung and former Xero engineer Jacob Duligall, and is now headquartered in San Francisco. In January 2026 it raised a US$55m Series B led by Blackbird, with participation from Icehouse Ventures, at a reported ~US$355m valuation. Customers include Uber, Shopify, Canva, Reddit, IBM, Eventbrite, Pinterest and Fonterra.

nodes.name: Wayve (Wayve Technologies Ltd)
nodes.subtitle: Embodied-AI self-driving company co-founded by NZ's Alex Kendall; Icehouse Ventures-backed

metadata.bio: Wayve is a London-headquartered autonomous-driving company that uses end-to-end deep learning ("embodied AI") to build a general-purpose self-driving intelligence from cameras rather than HD maps. It was founded in Cambridge, England in 2017 by Amar Shah and New Zealander Alex Kendall, who has been sole CEO since Shah's 2020 departure. In February 2026 it raised a US$1.2b Series D (US$1.5b total capital including Uber milestone funding) at an US$8.6b valuation, with Uber naming Wayve to power its first robotaxi fleet. New Zealand's Icehouse Ventures was a named investor in that round (NZ$12.5m, per NZ Herald), backing Kiwi founder Kendall.
metadata.statusDetail: Active private company; raised a US$1.2b Series D (Feb 2026) at an US$8.6b valuation; ~US$1.5b total capital secured including Uber milestone-based commitment
metadata.fundingNotable: US$1.2b Series D (Feb 2026), with ~US$1.5b total capital secured; led by Eclipse, Balderton and SoftBank Vision Fund 2, with strategic investors Mercedes-Benz, Nissan, Stellantis, Microsoft, Nvidia and Uber, and new institutional investors including Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, Baillie Gifford, British Business Bank, Schroders Capital and NZ's Icehouse Ventures (NZ$12.5m, per NZ Herald). Prior US$1.05b Series C (May 2024) led by SoftBank.
metadata.verifyNote: Founders, NZ origin, Icehouse backing and overall narrative all independently confirmed (Wayve's own Series D press release explicitly lists Icehouse Ventures as a new institutional investor; NZ Herald cites NZ$12.5m). Main correction: the draft called it a "US$1.5b Series D." Per Wayve's press release and CNBC, the Series D was US$1.2b at an US$8.6b valuation, with ~US$1.5b total capital secured including Uber's milestone-based commitment; reworded statusDetail, description and fundingNotable accordingly, and corrected the lead investors (Eclipse, Balderton, SoftBank Vision Fund 2 led; the automakers/tech firms were strategic investors). metadata.notes: The task premise that there is a separate "New Zealand company Wayve" is a misconception: there is only one self-driving Wayve (Wayve Technologies Ltd), HQ'd in London and founded in Cambridge, England in 2017. The NZ/Icehouse angle is that co-founder & CEO Alex Kendall is a Christchurch-raised New Zealander (University of Auckland grad), and Auckland-based Icehouse Ventures invested in Wayve's Feb 2026 round (NZ$12.5m per NZ Herald). So icehouseBacked is confirmed, but the company is UK-domiciled, not NZ-domiciled. Funding figures vary by source/currency: the US$1.5b total is reported in NZD as ~$2.5b (NZ Herald) and the Series D component as US$1.2b at US$8.6b valuation (Wayve press release, CNBC); one EU source framed it as ~EUR1b / EUR7.2b. nodes.name: Contented AI
nodes.subtitle: AI that turns recorded meetings and conversations into business-ready documents and insights

metadata.bio: Contented (Contented AI) is a Christchurch, New Zealand AI startup that captures meetings, video calls and in-person conversations and converts them into structured, business-ready documents and insights using customisable templates. Founded in 2023 by Lucy Pink and Hannah Hardy-Jones, it serves more than 200 organisations globally across professional services, wealth management, government, healthcare, construction and enterprise. The company reached roughly NZD $1.4m in annual recurring revenue without external investment before closing a $4.1m seed round in early 2026.
metadata.industry: Artificial Intelligence / SaaS (conversation intelligence & document generation)

nodes.name: Basis

nodes.name: Narrative
nodes.subtitle: AI-powered photo culling and editing software for professional photographers, built in Auckland, NZ.

metadata.bio: Narrative is an Auckland, New Zealand startup building AI-powered workflow software for professional photographers, best known for its image-culling tool Select and its Publish website builder. It was founded in 2017 by internationally known wedding photographer James Broadbent and software engineer Steffan Levet to cut the time photographers spend selecting their best shots. In July 2020 it raised a seed round of about US$2.58 million (roughly NZ$4 million) led by Peter Thiel's Founders Fund, with Icehouse Ventures participating, following an earlier ~NZ$700k angel round via The Icehouse's Flux Accelerator. The company remains active and operating.
metadata.statusDetail: Active and operating; raised a ~US$2.58M (≈NZ$4M) Founders Fund-led seed in July 2020. A reported ~$8.5M Series A (circa March 2026) is from a single aggregator and is likely a confusion with an unrelated same-named US data-marketplace company.
metadata.fundingNotable: ~2019 angel round (~NZ$700k) led by The Icehouse's Flux Accelerator with Founders Fund participating; July 2020 seed of US$2.58M (~NZ$4M) led by Founders Fund (Peter Thiel) with Icehouse Ventures participating. NZ Growth Capital Partners lists Narrative as a portfolio case study. A reported $8.5M Series A (Signalbase, ~March 2026) is unconfirmed and likely conflated with a different US company also named Narrative.
metadata.verifyNote: Founders, founding year (2017), Auckland HQ, product, active status, and Icehouse Ventures backing all independently confirmed. Corrections: (1) seed round was US$2.58M (≈NZ$4M), not "US$4M" — the draft conflated the USD and NZD figures into one inflated number; (2) the $8.5M Series A is single-sourced (Signalbase, with a wrong 2018 founding year) and very likely conflated with an unrelated US company (narrative.io's $8.5M Series A led by G20 Ventures), so stage downgraded from "Series A" to the last well-documented round, "Seed"; (3) Steffan Levet's title firmed to "Co-Founder, Co-CEO & Co-Head of Engineering" per Matchstiq; (4) confidence lowered from high to medium due to these issues. NZ Growth Capital Partners' specific round participation is not confirmed in primary seed coverage (only a portfolio case-study page), so phrasing was softened.
metadata.notes: Name disambiguation is the key risk: at least one unrelated US company is also called "Narrative" — notably narrative.io, a customer-data marketplace that raised an $8.5M Series A led by G20 Ventures (TechCrunch, Aug 2020). This profile is the Auckland photography-software company at narrative.so. The Signalbase "$8.5M Series A" entry (dated ~March 2026, with a wrong 2018 founding year and no investors) appears to be a likely conflation with that US data company and should not be relied on. Icehouse Ventures backing is firmly confirmed via the Flux Accelerator angel round and the 2020 seed (TechCrunch names IV as a participant), though the dedicated Icehouse showcase URL now returns 404.

nodes.name: LearnCoach
nodes.subtitle: NZ's most-used online tutorial platform helping secondary students prepare for NCEA exams.

metadata.bio: LearnCoach is a New Zealand EdTech company providing online video tutorials, lessons, activities and government-approved exams to help secondary-school students prepare for NCEA. It was founded in 2012 by former Otago Boys' High School maths teacher David Cameron (after a maths-explainer video he made went viral), alongside his brother Mark Cameron and his then-fiancee Deborah Lambie, and supports roughly 100,000+ students per year. It is described as New Zealand's first online provider government-approved to deliver the New Zealand Curriculum and offers a teacher management platform for monitoring student progress and administering online assessments.
metadata.statusDetail: Active, privately held. Listed in Icehouse Ventures' portfolio; no evidence of acquisition or closure as of 2026.
metadata.fundingNotable: Raised a NZ$4.5m pre-Series A in Sept 2020 (valuing the company at ~NZ$13.5m), led by Icehouse Ventures and the Impact Enterprise Fund, on top of a NZ$1.5m seed round in 2019 also led by Icehouse. Icehouse held an approximately 25% stake. Crunchbase lists total funding as roughly US$4.36m.
metadata.verifyNote: Corrected the founders: Deborah Lambie is independently confirmed as a co-founder (RNZ titled the founders 'Dave Cameron & Deborah Lambie'; multiple sources), so her null/uncertain fields were filled — she is a medical doctor, BMedSc Hons (bioethics), Master of Entrepreneurship, CFA charterholder, Miss World NZ 2015 and later investment banker, and David Cameron's then-fiancee/wife (not his wife from the outset). Mark Cameron confirmed as David's older brother with Publons (Clarivate-acquired) background. David Cameron's role normalised to 'Co-founder & CEO'. Funding (NZ$4.5m pre-Series A Sept 2020 at ~NZ$13.5m led by Icehouse Ventures + Impact Enterprise Fund, atop NZ$1.5m 2019 seed, ~25% Icehouse stake), Icehouse backing, active status, 2012 founding, and the description/oneLiner all confirmed accurate. Could not load the LinkedIn profiles or Crunchbase directly to verify those URLs; Deborah Lambie's LinkedIn left null.
metadata.notes: Founding year is 2012 per LearnCoach's own About page and award sources; the Icehouse Ventures job board lists 2016 (likely an incorporation/profile artifact) and an RNZ piece loosely said 2013 — 2012 is treated as authoritative. Three co-founders are now independently confirmed: David Cameron (CEO), Mark Cameron (CTO, David's brother), and Deborah Lambie. This is the New Zealand LearnCoach (learncoach.com); not the same-named foreign coaching/education products. Funding figures are in NZ dollars.

nodes.name: Feed My Furbaby
nodes.subtitle: NZ subscription service delivering customised, locally-made natural dog food to your door

metadata.bio: Feed My Furbaby (now branded myFurbaby) is an Auckland-based pet food subscription business founded in 2017 by husband-and-wife team Ben and Amy Rennell after repeatedly running out of food for their dog, Jack. Customers answer a few questions about their dog online and receive a tailored, customisable feeding plan with premium, New Zealand-made natural dog food delivered on a repeat schedule. The company emphasises sustainability, marketing roughly 60% less plastic than traditional pet food packaging and operating as plastic neutral. It trades under the legal entity Animal Instinct Limited.
metadata.statusDetail: Operating; sells direct-to-consumer in NZ primarily under the myFurbaby brand (legacy domain feedmyfurbaby.co.nz). Website live and active with recent activity as of 2025-2026.
metadata.fundingNotable: Began with a Kickstarter campaign (Nov 2017) that finished at ~110% of its NZ$5,000 goal (confirmed by NZ Herald). Later received institutional backing from Icehouse Ventures: NZ Herald reported that Icehouse Ventures' women-led ArcAngels II fund "had already invested in online pet food delivery company Feed My Furbaby." Third-party aggregators (PitchBook/Tracxn) report roughly NZ$250K raised, but the exact amount is not confirmed by a primary source.

nodes.name: Datch
nodes.subtitle: Voice and AI assistant for industrial frontline workers to capture data and diagnose assets hands-free.

Founded in the UK in 2018 by Australian Mark Fosdike and New Zealanders Aric Thorn and Ben Purcell, the now US-based company integrates with enterprise asset management systems and has expanded into AI-driven asset insights. It has raised roughly US$28.7M and maintains New Zealand engineering offices in Auckland and Christchurch alongside US offices in New York and San Francisco.
metadata.statusDetail: Active in 2026 (~34 employees); closed a US$15M Series A extension led by Third Prime in August 2024, coinciding with the launch of its Asset Insights product, and continues operating across the US, NZ and Europe.

NZ fund Tuhua Ventures); Series A US$10M (July 2022, led by Blackhorn Ventures); Series A extension to US$15M (Aug 2024, led by Third Prime). nodes.name: Groov
nodes.subtitle: NZ mental wellbeing platform (formerly Mentemia), co-founded by Sir John Kirwan

metadata.bio: Groov is a New Zealand digital mental wellbeing company founded in 2018 as Mentemia and rebranded to Groov in March 2022. It was co-founded by former All Black and mental health advocate Sir John Kirwan and tech entrepreneur Adam Clark, offering a consumer wellbeing app alongside paid workplace wellbeing programmes for corporate clients. The company has since evolved toward science-based products including Groov Health (a care platform extending patient support between clinical appointments) and PerformanceCare (an organisational/workforce intelligence platform). Matt Krogstad is the current CEO; Kirwan and Clark remain co-founders on the board.
metadata.statusDetail: Active. Has evolved from a consumer/workplace wellbeing app into products including Groov Health (for healthcare providers) and PerformanceCare (for enterprises). No acquisition or closure found.
metadata.fundingNotable: Raised a Series A in May 2021 led by ACC's Impact Fund, with Pathfinder KiwiSaver, Icehouse Ventures and Sir Stephen Tindall's K One W One (K1W1) participating. Per BusinessDesk's cap-table reporting: Kirwan (with wife Fiorella) ~27.6% and Adam Clark's trustee company (Sheaf) ~27.6%, ACC Impact Fund ~11.5%, Icehouse Ventures 6.5%, Pathfinder ~3.2% (NZ$800k), K1W1 3%. ACC investment undisclosed but within the Impact Fund's NZ$2m-$15m band. Also received NZ Ministry of Health (COVID-19 response) funding to keep the consumer app free.
metadata.verifyNote: Fresh searches confirmed all major claims: co-founders Sir John Kirwan and Adam Clark (Clark's M-Com/Fiserv-2011 background verified via Businesswire/Fiserv); 2018 founding (BusinessDesk); March 2022 rebrand from Mentemia; May 2021 Series A led by ACC Impact Fund with Icehouse Ventures (6.5%), Pathfinder and K1W1; Icehouse backing CONFIRMED; cap table matches BusinessDesk; status active with Groov Health/PerformanceCare evolution; current CEO Matt Krogstad confirmed on team page. Current CEO per the team page is Matt Krogstad; Adam Clark was the founding CEO and remains a co-founder/board member. Aaron Tregaskis is listed as a board member (not a founder). Series A amount not publicly disclosed. Adam Clark's LinkedIn URL not confirmed, left null.

nodes.name: Nectar (Nectar Money / Nectar NZ Limited)
nodes.subtitle: NZ digital lender: 100% online personal loans with 7-minute decisions and same-day funding.

metadata.bio: Nectar (Nectar Money / Nectar NZ Limited) is an Auckland-based fintech operating a fully digital, 100%-online personal-loan platform for New Zealand consumers, with loan decisions in as little as 7 minutes and same-day funding. It offers personal, car, debt-consolidation and emergency loans (up to about NZ$37,500, average around NZ$11,500) and was the first NZ digital lender to release an API for broker applications. The company reports having originated more than NZ$100 million in loans since launch and is funded by both equity and debt investors. It remains active and registered as of 2026.

Icehouse Ventures Nominees Ltd appears as a shareholder on the NZ company register.

nodes.name: Melodics
nodes.subtitle: Gamified app for learning keys, pad controllers and drums - a "Duolingo" for music practice.

metadata.bio: Melodics is an Auckland, New Zealand-based music-technology company that makes software teaching people to play MIDI keyboards, pad controllers (finger drumming) and electronic drums. Its app delivers game-styled lessons, analyses the user's playing and gives real-time feedback on timing, rhythm and accuracy to keep practice engaging. It was conceived in 2014 by former Serato CEO Sam Gribben after he left Serato, and launched in October 2015. The platform reports a community of over 1,000,000 registered musicians worldwide.
metadata.statusDetail: Active and independent; reports 1,000,000+ registered musicians and ongoing product development (e.g. the "Songs" feature and current mobile apps). Series A was launched in 2019; no public exit or closure reported.
metadata.fundingNotable: Closed a US$1.2M round in September 2017 led by Berlin-based Ableton, with 500 Startups, NZ funds Tuhua Ventures and K1W1, and Harmonix co-founder Alex Rigopulos; a Series A followed (launched 2019). PitchBook/Tracxn report roughly US$2.89M total raised; figures vary by tracker.

nodes.name: Inhibit Coatings Limited
nodes.subtitle: NZ deep-tech making bound-silver-nanoparticle antimicrobial paints and coatings for food, health and high-touch surfaces

metadata.bio: Inhibit Coatings is a Wellington, New Zealand advanced-materials company founded in November 2016 to commercialise antimicrobial coating technology developed at Victoria University of Wellington. Its proprietary "smart chemistry" permanently binds silver nanoparticles into polymer-based coatings, giving low-leaching, long-lifetime antimicrobial and antiviral surfaces reported to kill over 650 microorganisms (including Listeria, E. coli and S. aureus). Applications span food processing, healthcare/aged care, flooring and plastics. The company has raised funding from NZ angel and venture investors and won a 2020 KiwiNet research-commercialisation award.
metadata.statusDetail: Active and operating as of 2025: website live, team page lists CEO/founder plus technical, operations and board members, ongoing R&D and commercialisation; no acquisition or closure reported.
metadata.fundingNotable: Reported ~NZ$2.5M raised across multiple rounds, including a ~NZ$1.5M raise to scale to commercial-size batches. Investors named across sources include Matū, Enterprise Angels, Angel HQ, Aspire NZ Seed Fund, New Zealand Growth Capital Partners, Powerhouse Ventures, Plug and Play and Icehouse Ventures. Grants include ~NZ$350k from MBIE's COVID-19 Innovation Accelerator Fund and ~NZ$200k from NZ Innovation Booster (NZIB). Exact totals and round structure are not authoritatively confirmed.

nodes.name: Rocos
nodes.subtitle: Cloud platform to connect, monitor and operate robots remotely; acquired by DroneDeploy in 2021.

metadata.bio: Rocos was an Auckland, New Zealand robot operations platform that gave robotics companies a cloud backend to connect, monitor and remotely control fleets of robots. Founded in 2017 by David Inggs and Richard Stinear, its software was deployed on robots such as Boston Dynamics' Spot for use cases including agriculture, vineyards and hazardous-environment data capture. In 2021 the company was acquired by US-based DroneDeploy to extend its jobsite automation from aerial drones to ground robots. Terms were undisclosed but reported as an "eight-figure" sum, and operations remained in New Zealand.

nodes.name: Joyous
nodes.subtitle: AI-powered conversational workforce feedback platform - "the Anti-Survey"

metadata.bio: Joyous is an Auckland, New Zealand SaaS company founded in 2017 by brothers Mike and Philip Carden that provides an AI-powered conversational feedback platform for large enterprises, positioning itself as "the Anti-Survey" alternative to traditional anonymous surveys. The platform lets organizations chat one-on-one with workers at scale, analyzes responses for actionable insights, and generates prioritized action plans. Named customers include large global organizations such as AT&T, KFC, Nokia, Taco Bell and Vodafone. The product was originally at joyoushq.com and now operates under the bejoyous.ai domain with a generative-AI focus.

nodes.name: Dexibit
nodes.subtitle: Big data and AI analytics for visitor attractions, museums and galleries

metadata.bio: Dexibit is an Auckland, New Zealand software company providing big data analytics and AI for visitor attractions such as museums, galleries, theme parks and stadiums. Its SaaS platform connects venue operating systems and external data to forecast and analyse visitor behaviour through dashboards, automated reporting and insights. Customers include leading cultural institutions such as the Smithsonian American Art Museum and London's National Gallery, with offices in Auckland, London and Washington DC. In late March 2026 Dexibit was acquired by UK-listed accesso Technology Group for NZ$20.9m (about US$12.1m).

The company built a pre-commercial demonstration plant in Auckland and aims to license and scale its technology with global steel-industry partners. It signed its first commercial deal with Chinese steelmaker Tranvic Group and was a recipient of Callaghan Innovation's inaugural Ārohia Innovation Trailblazer grant.

It uses the magnesium hydroxide to capture and mineralise industrial CO2 emissions into stable carbonates, aiming to decarbonise hard-to-abate industries while reducing critical-mineral supply-chain risk. In March 2025 it opened a critical-minerals pilot production plant in Christchurch, and in May 2025 announced plans for a first commercial-scale facility in Washington State, USA.

nodes.name: Foundry Lab

Founded in 2018 in Wellington by industrial designer David Moodie, it emerged from stealth in November 2021 with a US$8M Series A led by Blackbird. It targets defense, aerospace and automotive customers across alloys including aluminium, zinc, brass and stainless steel. In November 2024 it announced its first commercial sale, supplying a DMC-3 system to the New Jersey Innovation Institute under a US Army DEVCOM Armaments Center (COMET) initiative.

nodes.name: BioLumic

metadata.bio: BioLumic is a New Zealand- and US-based agritech company that applies precise, short-duration ultraviolet (UV) light treatments to seeds to activate beneficial, non-GMO plant traits that improve crop yield, vigour and resilience. Founded in 2013 by plant UV photobiologist Dr Jason Wargent out of his research at Massey University, it runs its patented "xTraits" light-signalling platform from Palmerston North, New Zealand, with US operations. In 2025 it launched commercial light-activated corn seed traits (with US deployment targeted for the 2026 planting season), began expanding into South America, and announced a multi-year forage/ryegrass partnership with Fonterra. Field trials with Fonterra are slated to start in 2026, with a commercial pasture product targeted for 2028.

metadata.bio: Nanolayr is an Auckland, New Zealand advanced-materials manufacturer that produces high-performance nanofibre textiles at industrial scale using an electrospinning process at its Mangere Bridge plant. The company was placed into voluntary administration in October 2025 after being unable to secure sufficient investment to reach profitable commercial revenue scale.

metadata.bio: Preno is a New Zealand cloud-based hotel management software company serving boutique hotels, motels, and lodges. Co-founded by Amelia Gain (CEO) and Max Podolian (CTO), the product launched to market in late 2015 and is used by independent hoteliers across more than 20 countries. The company remains active and privately held, headquartered in Auckland with a London presence.

nodes.name: NILO (NILO Limited)
nodes.subtitle: NZ cleantech turning waste plastic into low-carbon adhesives for engineered wood

metadata.bio: NILO is an Auckland-based cleantech / deep tech company that upcycles hard-to-recycle polyethylene (PE) and polypropylene (PP) plastic waste into an industrial adhesive. The binder is positioned as a drop-in replacement for the urea formaldehyde used in engineered wood products such as particle board, MDF and plywood, cutting formaldehyde off-gassing and carbon emissions. In 2023 Inter IKEA Group took a 12.5% stake and a board seat, then co-led a NZ$13m Series A in December 2024 alongside Pacific Channel. The company says it had previously raised about NZ$15m from investors including Icehouse Ventures and Sir Stephen Tindall's K1W1.

nodes.name: Parrot Analytics

metadata.bio: Parrot Analytics is a data science company that measures and predicts global audience demand for TV shows, films and other entertainment content across streaming, social media and other platforms, built around its "Demand Expressions" metric. Founded in New Zealand by Wared Seger (who grew up in West Auckland and drew on the University of Auckland entrepreneurship ecosystem), it became a leading provider of cross-platform demand analytics for studios, broadcasters and streamers worldwide. The company is now headquartered in the Los Angeles / West Hollywood area, with additional offices including Auckland, New York and London. It remains an active, private, independent company as of 2026.

nodes.name: Vortex Power Systems
nodes.subtitle: NZ cleantech turning industrial waste heat into clean power via man-made atmospheric vortices

metadata.bio: Vortex Power Systems is a New Zealand deep-tech / cleantech company that grew out of research at the University of Auckland and converts low-grade industrial waste heat into zero-carbon electricity. Its proprietary system uses waste heat to saturate air and create a controlled, free-standing atmospheric buoyancy vortex (a man-made whirlwind) whose rising, swirling column of air drives a turbine to generate power. After proving the physics in the University of Auckland's aerodynamics lab, the company has broken ground on a pilot plant near Gisborne (Whangara) aimed at driving a roughly one-megawatt generator. It remains an early-stage, pre-revenue R&D company and has reportedly sought around NZ$5 million to build the demonstration plant at scale.

nodes.name: Upstock

metadata.bio: Upstock is a New Zealand-based B2B marketplace that simplifies wholesale food and beverage ordering between suppliers and buyers such as cafes, restaurants, bars, grocers and supermarkets, replacing disorganised texts, emails and phone calls with a digital platform. It was started by Foxton Fizz owner Matt Watson and built out by former Xero team members Philip Fierlinger and Duncan Ritchie, who lead the company as co-CEOs. By 2024 it connected over 30,000 wholesale buyers to more than 1,000 suppliers and around 90,000 products across New Zealand and Australia. The company has expanded into Australia and signed a distribution deal with Woolworths.

nodes.name: Pyper Vision
nodes.subtitle: NZ aerospace startup using AI "fog-casting" to cut fog-related airport and airline delays

metadata.bio: Pyper Vision is a Christchurch, New Zealand aerospace startup founded by Emily Blythe that builds technology to reduce fog-related flight disruptions. It originally developed a drone-dispersed, water-absorbing (hygroscopic) system to clear fog, then pivoted around 2023 toward an AI/deep-learning "fog-casting" platform that aims to predict fog more accurately than traditional forecasts (which often warn of fog that never forms). The company has run trials and partnerships with Air New Zealand, Christchurch, Hamilton and Dunedin airports, and London City Airport (via BA CityFlyer). Fog is cited as causing billions of dollars in annual aviation losses worldwide.

nodes.name: Zethos (formerly Zincovery)

Its selective-reduction process runs at lower temperatures and can be powered by renewable electricity, reported to use about 70% less energy, cut carbon emissions by up to ~95%, and lower operating costs by up to ~50% versus conventional coal-based methods. In 2025 the company rebranded from Zincovery to Zethos to reflect a broader critical-minerals focus, and it has opened a roughly 2,500 sqm large-scale metal refining demonstration facility in Bromley, Christchurch. It raised a NZ$3m seed round in October 2022 with Icehouse Ventures as the largest investor, and reports total funding of roughly NZ$16-20m.

Founded in 2020 by Shaun Seaman and Jotinder Singh, the company operates out of Auckland while being registered/headquartered in Singapore to improve access to venture capital and Southeast Asian customers. In 2024 it raised over US$5 million (about NZ$8.5 million) in seed funding to build a pilot plant in Mount Roskill, Auckland.

nodes.name: Grater Goods
nodes.subtitle: NZ artisanal plant-based charcuterie, cheese and deli producer (in liquidation, Nov 2025).

metadata.bio: Grater Goods was a Christchurch-based New Zealand company making gourmet plant-based delicatessen products including vegan charcuterie, "meats," cheeses, spreads and pates, alongside a contract-manufacturing arm and a vegan bistro. It was founded in 2018 by musician-turned-entrepreneur Clare "Flip" Grater and her French husband Youssef Iskrane, pitching itself as a European-style plant-based deli first-mover. The business was placed into voluntary liquidation on 7 November 2025 after a Woolworths supply deal lined up in early 2024 was put on hold and ultimately lost, leaving a working-capital squeeze. Flip Grater described the company as "simply a victim of the current economy."

metadata.fundingNotable: Icehouse Ventures' ArcAngels fund (women-led startups) invested NZ$80,000 in a 2021 pre-seed round, holding an 8.29% minority stake among 11 shareholders at liquidation. The technology was originally developed at Callaghan Innovation, and the greenhouse application is now commercialised through a partner called Aplenty. The company operated a commercial unit at the Gourmet Mokai greenhouse near Taupo and is broadening into adjacent uses such as hydrogen production and gas cleaning.

The company is extending its technology to direct lithium extraction (DLE), with a pre-commercial demonstration plant funded in 2025 for North American deployment, and is exploring recovery of other minerals such as boron and caesium. Founded in 2010 as Environmetals Limited, it rebranded to Geo40 in 2017.

nodes.name: Neocrete
nodes.subtitle: NZ cleantech making a concrete additive that cuts cement use 30-50% to lower emissions

metadata.bio: Neocrete is a New Zealand cleantech startup decarbonising concrete. Its core product, the Neocrete Activator, is a powder additive (about 3% of cementitious material) that "supercharges" abundant low-carbon materials such as volcanic ash, fly ash and steel slag so they can replace 30-50% of the cement in concrete without losing strength. The technology builds on roughly 20 years of concrete-additive research by co-founder Zarina Bazoeva's father, Russian civil-engineering professor Dr Oleg Bazoev, and the company aims to produce cement-free, zero-carbon concrete by 2027. It has been used on NZ projects (including the Kāinga Ora Bader Ventura housing development), operates labs in Parnell and a manufacturing plant in South Auckland, and was selected for CRH Ventures' 2025 Sustainable Building Materials Accelerator.
metadata.statusDetail: Active. Raised a US$4m (NZ$6.5m) seed round announced 26 March 2024; operates labs/offices in Parnell and a manufacturing plant in South Auckland, runs international pilot/testing programmes, and was selected for CRH Ventures' 2025 Sustainable Building Materials Accelerator.

nodes.subtitle: NZ medtech building a tiny battery-free implantable pressure sensor, first for hydrocephalus

metadata.bio: Kitea Health is an Auckland-based medtech company developing miniature, battery-free implantable digital pressure sensors for managing chronic conditions. Its lead clinical application is hydrocephalus (monitoring brain pressure and shunt function), with longer-term plans for heart failure via pulmonary artery pressure monitoring; the rice-grain-sized sensor is read by a wireless wand and app. Spun out of the University of Auckland's Auckland Bioengineering Institute in May 2022, it implanted sensors in adults at Auckland Hospital from mid-2024 and reported a world-first implant in a child with hydrocephalus in January 2025. The device is not yet approved for clinical use and the company is preparing for human trials in the US.
metadata.statusDetail: Active and privately held; closed an oversubscribed NZ$13m pre-Series A round (December 2025) and is preparing for human trials in the US. Device not yet approved for clinical use.
metadata.fundingNotable: NZ$6m seed round in 2023 (led by Pacific Channel; Icehouse Ventures, Auckland UniServices, Cure Kids Ventures, NZGCP and angels also participated); oversubscribed NZ$13m pre-Series A round closed December 2025 led by Icehouse Ventures, with Sydney-based health-tech VCs Bioshore and Karst Peak Rx (KP Rx). Also received ~NZ$14m in research grants (including a 2017 MBIE Endeavour fund grant).

nodes.name: Factor (Prospero Energy Limited)
nodes.subtitle: AI forecasting and pricing engine for energy retailers; acquired by Gentrack in 2026.

metadata.bio: Factor (legal entity Prospero Energy Limited) is a Wellington, New Zealand energy-tech startup that builds AI-powered forecasting and pricing software for energy retailers and utilities. Its platform replaces legacy spreadsheet-based processes with tools to price and manage complex commercial electricity contracts at scale using machine learning over large datasets. It was founded by ex-Flick Electric / Flux Federation team members and raised around NZ$3 million in a round led by Icehouse Ventures. In May 2026 it was acquired by NZX/ASX-listed energy software firm Gentrack.
metadata.statusDetail: Acquired by Gentrack (NZX/ASX: GTK) at NZ$24m enterprise value, plus a potential earn-out of up to NZ$10m tied to growing annual recurring revenue to ~NZ$17m over three years. Sale and purchase agreement signed and completed simultaneously on 15 May 2026.

nodes.name: Miruku
nodes.subtitle: Molecular-farming startup growing real dairy proteins and fats in oilseed crops, no cows required.

metadata.bio: Miruku is a New Zealand biotech/agritech startup using "molecular farming" to produce real dairy proteins, fats and sugars inside specially designed oilseed crops (notably safflower) rather than from cows. Its proprietary Dairy Seed System aims to supply animal-free dairy ingredients via existing agricultural infrastructure. Founded in 2020, it positions molecular farming as a more scalable alternative to precision fermentation. The company runs crop trials with farming partners and works toward regulatory approvals and co-developed products with food-industry partners.

nodes.name: Caruso
nodes.subtitle: AI-native fund administration and registry software for private-markets fund managers.

metadata.bio: Caruso is a New Zealand-founded B2B fintech that combines AI-native software with fund administration services for real estate, private credit, and private equity fund managers, spanning CRM, registry, compliance, capital raising, distributions, and investor portals. It was spun out of commercial real estate firm Jasper in early 2023, where the technology had been built in-house over three years before being offered to third-party managers. By its 2026 Series A, the platform was used by more than 80 fund managers running around 900 funds across Australia, New Zealand, and the US. It operates offices in Auckland, Sydney, and Dallas.

nodes.name: ANDFOODS
nodes.subtitle: NZ foodtech making plant-based dairy-free creams from legume pulses via fermentation.

The company spun out of research at Massey University and the Riddet Institute and targets professional foodservice and food-manufacturing applications. In March 2024 it raised a NZ$2.7 million seed round led by Icehouse Ventures. Former Synlait CEO Leon Clement chairs the company.

nodes.name: Kwetta
nodes.subtitle: NZ power-electronics startup unlocking ultra-fast EV charging by tapping grid capacity directly.

metadata.bio: Kwetta is a Napier, New Zealand-based energy technology startup founded in 2021 that develops power electronics for ultra-fast EV charging. Its flagship Prime Grid Gateway connects directly to the medium/high-voltage distribution grid, unlocking up to ten times more power at constrained sites without costly grid upgrades or large battery storage. The company targets heavy transport, fleets and large charging hubs, and has partnered with Z Energy to roll out ultra-fast chargers across NZ service stations. In 2024 it closed an oversubscribed Series A led by Blackbird, with Icehouse Ventures, Virescent Ventures and Z Energy also backing the company; it is now expanding into Australia and Europe (with an Amsterdam office).
metadata.statusDetail: Operating and scaling; 30+ employees across New Zealand and Australia, with a Netherlands (Amsterdam) office, expanding to Australia and Europe following its 2024 Series A.

nodes.name: AF Drinks
nodes.subtitle: NZ alcohol-free adult RTD cocktail brand with its proprietary Afterglow warming botanical.

nodes.name: Alimetry
nodes.subtitle: NZ medtech behind Gastric Alimetry, a non-invasive wearable for diagnosing gut disorders.

metadata.bio: Alimetry is a New Zealand medical technology company that develops Gastric Alimetry, a non-invasive, wearable device performing body-surface gastric mapping to diagnose neuromuscular and sensory gut disorders. A flexible electrode array applied to the abdomen measures the stomach's electrical activity through the skin, with cloud and AI-based analysis aiding clinicians. It is a University of Auckland / Auckland Bioengineering Institute spinout founded in 2019, built on roughly a decade of gut electrophysiology research. The flagship product has received multiple US FDA clearances and is used by 40-plus hospitals and clinics worldwide.
metadata.statusDetail: Active and commercializing; the flagship Gastric Alimetry device has multiple US FDA clearances and 40-plus hospitals and clinics globally have signed on to use it. Operates across New Zealand, the US and the UK, with the US the primary expansion market.

Prior rounds include a ~US$3.3M seed and a NZ$16.3M Series A (March 2022) led by Movac, with IP Group, UniServices, Matu Karihi and K1W1 participating.
