metadata.priorBackground: Previously a manager at Mighty River Power (NZ energy company); conceived AskNicely after observing Uber's instant post-ride feedback loop.

metadata.bio: John Ballinger co-founded AskNicely in 2014 and serves as CTO, leading product development from New Zealand. He is the technical co-founder who built the company's platform.
metadata.priorBackground: Studied Engineering Science (Engineer's Degree) at the University of Auckland (1996-2000); software developer and also a founder of e-signature platform GoodSign.

metadata.bio: Former corporate lawyer at Bell Gully in Auckland who left law in 2021 to teach himself to code and build Ivo. Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia (2024).
metadata.priorBackground: Studied at the University of Auckland; practised as a corporate solicitor at Bell Gully (Auckland).

metadata.bio: Technical co-founder of Ivo, leading engineering for its AI contract review and intelligence platform.
metadata.priorBackground: Former senior software engineer at Xero in Wellington.

nodes.name: Alex Kendall
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & CEO, Wayve (Wayve Technologies Ltd)
nodes.location: London, United Kingdom (raised in Christchurch, New Zealand)

metadata.bio: New Zealander (Christchurch-raised, University of Auckland mechatronics engineering grad) who founded Wayve out of his Cambridge PhD research on end-to-end deep learning for self-driving. Originally CTO, he became CEO in 2020. Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 and appointed OBE in 2025 for services to AI.
metadata.priorBackground: BE(Hons) mechatronics, University of Auckland; PhD in deep learning, computer vision and robotics at University of Cambridge (Woolf Fisher Scholar); Fellow of Trinity College, Cambridge (2017). Personal site alexgkendall.com.

nodes.name: Amar Shah
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder (initial CEO; departed 2020), Wayve (Wayve Technologies Ltd)

metadata.bio: Machine-learning PhD from the University of Cambridge (Zoubin Ghahramani's Machine Learning group). Co-founded Wayve in 2017 and initially served as CEO, departing the company in 2020.
metadata.priorBackground: PhD in machine learning, University of Cambridge (Zoubin Ghahramani's group).

metadata.bio: Self-taught developer who previously founded ethical-fashion startup Onyou. At Contented she focuses on product and software development.
metadata.priorBackground: Founder of Onyou (ethical fashion startup); self-taught developer.

metadata.bio: Christchurch entrepreneur who previously founded The Kite Program, a mental health app. She has a background in HR and co-founded Contented around a shared interest in business applications of AI.
metadata.priorBackground: Founder of The Kite Program (mental health app); University of Canterbury alumna (BA, GDipHRM); background in HR.

metadata.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Mint Innovation, leading the company since 2016. Holds a BSc and PhD in Chemistry from the University of Leicester. Also associated with NZ deeptech incubator Outset Ventures.
metadata.priorBackground: Spent about seven years at clean-tech company LanzaTech as VP of External Affairs, leading legal and intellectual property teams, before founding Mint in 2016. Chairperson of KiwiNet. PhD in Chemistry, University of Leicester.

nodes.name: Ollie Crush
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & Chief Science Officer, Mint Innovation

metadata.bio: Co-founder and Chief Science Officer of Mint Innovation, leading the company's science and bioprocess development since 2016. Holds a PhD in Biotechnology from the University of Cambridge and a BAppSc in Molecular Biotechnology from the University of Otago.
metadata.priorBackground: PhD in Biotechnology, University of Cambridge; BAppSc in Molecular Biotechnology, University of Otago. Research associate at Imperial College London; executive council member of BIOTech New Zealand; named NZBIO Young Bioscientist of the Year 2017.

metadata.bio: Co-founded Spalk in 2015 after commentating sports online with co-founders and building a following, and leads the company as CEO. Named in the University of Auckland's 40 Under 40 alumni list.
metadata.priorBackground: Bachelor of Commerce, University of Auckland; took part in the university's Velocity programme and Vodafone Xone incubator.

metadata.bio: Co-founded Spalk in 2015 and serves as CTO, leading product and engineering from the Auckland office. Described in early coverage as the team's lead engineer.
metadata.priorBackground: Engineering graduate, University of Auckland.

metadata.bio: An original co-founder of Spalk alongside Reynolds and Prendergast; early NZ coverage (Stuff, Newshub, Idealog) names him as part of the founding trio. He left the company around 2016 and is now founder and CMO of marketing agency UTTR.
metadata.priorBackground: University of Auckland; co-founded Spalk while a student, later founded UTTR.

metadata.bio: West Auckland electrician who founded Tradify after becoming frustrated by the admin and paperwork of running his electrical business. He led the company as CEO until mid-2020, when Michael Steckler took over, and continued as a board director; he held about 9% of the company ahead of the 2024 acquisition.
metadata.priorBackground: Electrician / electrical engineering background; left school for an electrical apprenticeship in South Auckland and ran his own electrical business before building Tradify.

metadata.bio: James co-founded Hnry with his wife Claire after experiencing the tax and financial admin burden of being self-employed. He leads the company as CEO and has driven its expansion into Australia and the UK.
metadata.priorBackground: English-born; trained as a developer before moving into technology management consultancy, with senior roles at firms including Deloitte, Thomson Reuters, Davanti and Westpac.

metadata.bio: Claire co-founded Hnry with James and serves as Chief Operating Officer, helping scale the company across New Zealand, Australia and the UK.
metadata.priorBackground: Background in finance, compliance, legal and data analysis; previously worked as a consultant in New Zealand (including for EQC and MPI) before co-founding Hnry.

metadata.bio: James Donald is co-founder and CEO of Ideally, with a background in startups and product development in New Zealand's tech sector.
metadata.priorBackground: Co-founded NZ tourism-tech SaaS company Yonder (customer service/sales tool for tour operators), which was acquired by TOMIS in June 2024. Bachelor of Engineering (Hons) and Bachelor of Commerce in Economics, University of Auckland.

metadata.bio: Brendan Cervin is co-founder and CTO of Ideally, a SaaS technology leader with nearly two decades as a startup CTO.
metadata.priorBackground: Co-founder/CTO of GeoOp; later CTO at ArchiPro and Yabble, and roles at Whip Around and Head of Software and Data at Tru-Test Group. Bachelor of Engineering (software), University of Auckland.

metadata.bio: Joshua Nu'u-Steele is co-founder and Chief Revenue Officer of Ideally, leading its commercial growth and now its New York office and US expansion.
metadata.priorBackground: Led international sales expansion at Parkable (Global/National Sales Manager) and earlier drove growth for Booking.com in New Zealand. Bachelor of Business (International Business & Management), AUT University.

metadata.bio: Co-founder of Basis and its original CEO; current sources name Alex Cappy as CEO (from 2024), so Purcell's present title is unclear. Co-founded the company in 2020 to digitise the home electrical switchboard.
metadata.priorBackground: Worked in investment / venture capital before founding Basis; specific prior employer varies across sources (NZ Growth Capital Partners and ACC's investment arm have both been cited).

metadata.bio: Co-founder of Basis and an electrical controls expert, described in NZ media as a former electrician. Co-founded the company with Danny Purcell in 2020 after the two met and shared frustration with the energy sector.
metadata.priorBackground: Electrical controls expert and former project manager at Laser Electrical; former electrician.

nodes.name: Dave Ferguson
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & Co-CEO (formerly President), Nuro, Inc.
nodes.location: San Francisco Bay Area, USA (originally New Zealand)

metadata.bio: New Zealand-born roboticist who co-founded Nuro in 2016 after working as a principal engineer on Google's self-driving car project (now Waymo). Named Co-CEO of Nuro in October 2025, focusing on capital and commercial partnerships. Won a Kea World Class New Zealand Award in 2022.
metadata.priorBackground: BSc in computer science and mathematics from the University of Otago (New Zealand); MS and PhD in Robotics from Carnegie Mellon University; principal engineer at Google's self-driving project (Waymo); led the planning group for CMU's 2007 DARPA Urban Challenge-winning team; PhD-era code used on Mars rovers.

metadata.bio: Co-founded Nuro in 2016 after serving as a principal software engineer and founding team member of Google's self-driving car project (now Waymo), where he led the perception and simulation teams. Leads Nuro's product and technology and is Co-CEO alongside Dave Ferguson (since October 2025).
metadata.priorBackground: Principal software engineer and founding team member at Google's self-driving car project (Waymo); led perception and simulation efforts.

metadata.bio: Auckland-based entrepreneur who founded PowerbyProxi in 2007 out of his University of Auckland engineering work and led it as CEO until the 2017 Apple acquisition. After the acquisition he became Managing Director of Apple's Auckland Technology Centre, and was recognised as a Kea World Class New Zealander.
metadata.priorBackground: University of Auckland engineering student; placed second in the 2003 Spark $40k (Velocity) Challenge with his 4th-year project on wireless power; emigrated from Bahrain and attended Auckland Grammar School; worked with University of Auckland wireless power academics.

metadata.bio: Co-founded PowerbyProxi after entering the 2003 Spark $40k Challenge with Fady Mishriki, where they placed second and won time at The Icehouse. He served in an engineering leadership role and, after the Apple acquisition, became an Engineering Manager at Apple. Named in the University of Auckland 40 Under 40 alumni.
metadata.priorBackground: University of Auckland Bachelor of Engineering graduate; emigrated from Oman and attended Auckland Grammar School with Mishriki; ~3.5 years at Fisher & Paykel Healthcare from 2004 before joining PowerbyProxi.

metadata.bio: Experienced New Zealand technology entrepreneur introduced to Mishriki and Bhargava through The Icehouse, with whom he co-founded PowerbyProxi in 2007. He is also known for co-founding AI company Soul Machines.
metadata.priorBackground: Veteran NZ tech entrepreneur and executive; met the founders via The Icehouse network.

metadata.bio: Founder and CEO of Migrate Mate. Of Serbian heritage and raised in Australia, he moved to the US and faced repeated visa-related job rejections (reportedly 26) before starting the company. Featured on Forbes 30 Under 30 for Social Impact.
metadata.priorBackground: Studied Finance and Economics at the University of Western Australia; worked in the US on various work visas before founding Migrate Mate.

metadata.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Migrate Mate, described as Bozic's best friend who built the product. He was based in London when the company was started. Limited additional public detail confirmed.

Co-founded LawVu in 2015 in Tauranga and serves as CEO. Before LawVu he worked in the project-management software world, where he encountered the problem LawVu set out to solve. He continues to lead the company through its global expansion and AI push.
metadata.priorBackground: Earlier worked at a startup in the project-management / accounting-software space (reported as integrating accounting software with NZ Inland Revenue systems); based in Tauranga, NZ.

nodes.name: Tim Boyne
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder (former Chief Strategy Officer); departed c.2022, LawVu

metadata.bio: Co-founded LawVu in 2015 after about a decade working in the IT team at Tauranga law firm Sharp Tudhope, which informed the idea for in-house legal software. He left LawVu around 2022 and is now CEO of SmartSpace.ai; his LinkedIn still shows a former Co-Founder & CSO title.
metadata.role: Co-founder (former Chief Strategy Officer); departed c.2022
metadata.priorBackground: Around 10 years in the IT operations team at NZ law firm Sharp Tudhope; later CEO of SmartSpace.ai.

metadata.bio: Engineer who worked on Rocket Lab's senior engineering team before co-founding Partly. EY Entrepreneur of the Year (NZ) finalist and recognised among New Zealand's leading young founders.
metadata.priorBackground: Engineer at Rocket Lab (Nasdaq: RKLB); founded several companies while studying engineering, including an earlier e-commerce venture with his Partly co-founders.

metadata.bio: Co-founder and Chief Operating Officer at Partly, leading operations and customer-facing teams.
metadata.priorBackground: Co-founded the founders' earlier e-commerce venture before Partly.

metadata.bio: Co-founder of Partly, leading the marketing function.
metadata.priorBackground: Co-founded the founders' earlier e-commerce venture before Partly.

metadata.bio: Co-founder and Head of Engineering at Partly; senior full-stack engineer.
metadata.priorBackground: Senior full-stack engineer; co-founded the founders' earlier e-commerce venture before Partly.

metadata.bio: CEO and co-founder of First AML. He studied engineering at the University of Auckland and became a registered patent attorney (AJ Park) before completing an MBA at Cambridge and working in strategy consulting at Bain & Company; he co-founded First AML in 2017/2018.
metadata.priorBackground: Bain & Company (strategy consulting); registered patent attorney at AJ Park; MBA, University of Cambridge; B.E. engineering, University of Auckland; former Strategy Manager, Air New Zealand

nodes.name: Bion Behdin
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & Chief Revenue Officer, First AML

metadata.bio: Co-founder and Chief Revenue Officer of First AML. A former corporate/commercial banker (about six years at ANZ Bank as a relationship manager) who experienced AML onboarding burdens firsthand, which inspired the company.
metadata.priorBackground: ~6 years at ANZ Bank in corporate/commercial banking (relationship manager); BA in Sociology and Classical Studies, University of Auckland

nodes.name: Chris Caigou
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & Chief Customer Officer, First AML

metadata.bio: Co-founder and Chief Customer Officer of First AML. A former corporate banker who, alongside Bion Behdin, encountered AML compliance friction before co-founding the company.
metadata.priorBackground: Former corporate banker

nodes.name: Dr Tom Williams
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & CEO, Number 8 Bio
nodes.location: Sydney, Australia (originally from Waikato, New Zealand)

metadata.bio: Synthetic biologist and CEO of Number 8 Bio. Raised in New Zealand's Waikato dairy region; trained in biochemistry and microbiology before moving into yeast metabolic engineering in Australia. Began ideating the company with Alex Carpenter in 2019, launching it in 2022.
metadata.priorBackground: BSc (biochemistry) and MSc (microbiology), University of Waikato; PhD in engineering yeast physiology and metabolism, University of Queensland; postdoc on the Yeast 2.0 project at Macquarie University (from 2015); later a group leader at Macquarie studying synthetic carbon metabolism, synthetic genomes and biosensors.

nodes.name: Dr Alex Carpenter
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & Chief Scientific Officer (CSO), Number 8 Bio

metadata.bio: Synthetic biologist and CSO of Number 8 Bio, focused on engineering microbes to cut livestock methane. Co-founded the company with Tom Williams, having earlier worked in Claudia Vickers's synthetic biology lab.
metadata.priorBackground: BSc in biomedical science, University of Queensland (shifting to metabolic engineering); Master of Research in Sydney; PhD on biosensors for directed evolution. Worked in Claudia Vickers's synthetic biology laboratory.

nodes.name: Adrian Macneil
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & CEO, Foxglove
nodes.location: San Francisco, USA (originally from New Zealand)

metadata.bio: New Zealander who co-founded Foxglove in 2021 and leads it as CEO. A Massey University computer science graduate whose first job was as a software engineer at the NZ Treasury before moving to Silicon Valley.
metadata.priorBackground: Massey University (computer science); first job as a software engineer at the NZ Treasury; later led Infrastructure at Cruise and was an early Director of Engineering at Coinbase before founding Foxglove.

metadata.bio: Co-founded Foxglove in 2021 with Adrian Macneil and serves as CTO, having worked alongside Macneil at both Cruise and Coinbase.
metadata.priorBackground: Software engineer at Cruise Automation and Coinbase (also prior roles including Polychain Labs) before co-founding Foxglove.

metadata.bio: New Zealand fintech entrepreneur who founded Genoapay (in market from August 2016) and led it through its 2018 acquisition by Latitude Financial Services. He later co-founded insurtech Simfuni, where he is CEO. He is also the second person, after his father, to complete a solo row across the Tasman Sea (Australia to New Zealand, 2010).
metadata.priorBackground: Background in payments and financial services; later co-founded insurtech Simfuni. Often cited with ~17 years of payments experience.

metadata.bio: Software engineer named by NZ business media (NBR, Startup Daily) as a co-founder of Genoapay alongside Shaun Quincey. He went on to co-found insurtech Simfuni as Chief Technology Officer. His specific founding title at Genoapay is not stated in primary sources, which name only Quincey as founder/CEO.
metadata.priorBackground: 20+ years in software engineering (design, architecture, development and compliance) across multiple countries; later CTO and co-founder of Simfuni.

metadata.bio: Founded Adherium (originally Nexus6) in 2001 to help manage his own asthma, developing the Smartinhaler connected-inhaler platform in his garage and leading the company through its 2015 ASX IPO until June 2017 (succeeded by Arik Anderson). He is named as an inventor across multiple Smartinhaler/Hailie patent families and is now CEO of gastrointestinal-device company The Insides Company.
metadata.priorBackground: MSc in Physics (First-Class Honours), University of Waikato, NZ. Prior roles at Microsoft and Gallagher Group; later founder/CEO of The Insides Company.

nodes.name: Mark Gatt
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & CEO, Thinkladder
nodes.location: Snells Beach, Auckland region, New Zealand

metadata.bio: Mark Gatt (full name Mark Barry Gatt) co-founded Thinkladder with his wife Kate and leads the company as CEO. The couple, based at Snells Beach near Auckland, set out to build a CBT app to make mental-health support more widely accessible.
metadata.priorBackground: Previously a project manager at Springboard Community Works (where he ran the Futureworks programme) before starting Thinkladder.

nodes.name: Kate Gatt
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder, Thinkladder
nodes.location: Snells Beach, Auckland region, New Zealand

metadata.bio: Kate (also reported as Katie) Gatt is a counsellor and co-founded Thinkladder with her husband Mark. She crafted the app's therapeutic content alongside additional therapists and is the clinical/content force behind its CBT-based approach.
metadata.priorBackground: Trained/practising counsellor; led therapeutic content development for the app with five additional therapists.

metadata.bio: Surgeon-engineer and obstetrician/gynaecologist who describes ~23 years in medicine. An advanced laparoscopic surgeon, she holds a Master's in Medical Engineering and is pursuing a PhD at the University of Melbourne in novel therapeutics and medical devices. She founded E-Leviate (via her entity Medical Devices & Technologies) to commercialise an estriol-eluting pessary ring for women's pelvic health.
metadata.priorBackground: Obstetrician and advanced laparoscopic/gynaecological surgeon in Auckland; Medical Engineer; PhD candidate at the University of Melbourne. Selected into SBE Australia's Life Sciences program.

metadata.bio: Co-founded VidApp in 2013 with Hannah Curd while travelling through Europe, after being asked to turn DVDs into video apps; leads the company as CEO. Brother of co-founder Rory Hancock.
metadata.priorBackground: Reported to hold an MBA from the University of Cambridge and a software-engineering background, and to have previously worked as a technical project manager at IBM (per the MemberPress profile).

metadata.bio: Co-founded VidApp in 2013 and leads mobile development; described as a self-taught coder who built much of the early platform.
metadata.priorBackground: BSc in Mathematics, Operations Research & Applied Statistics, Victoria University of Wellington (2002-2005). Prior analytics roles: Senior Campaign Analyst at St George Bank, Insight Analyst at Barclays Wealth, and Campaign Execution Analyst at Commonwealth Bank of Australia.

metadata.bio: Joined the founding team around 2016 to lead sales and marketing, ahead of the team entering Icehouse Ventures' Flux accelerator in 2017; serves as VP of Sales & Marketing. Brother of co-founder/CEO Dave Hancock.
metadata.priorBackground: Brother of CEO Dave Hancock; background in sales with education in finance and international business.

nodes.name: Greg O'Grady
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & Director (former CEO of predecessor Surgical Design Studio), The Insides Company

metadata.bio: Consultant colorectal surgeon and Associate Professor of Surgery at the University of Auckland; co-founded the company (as Surgical Design Studio) in 2017 and served as CEO until 2019, after which he focused on his other venture, Alimetry. He remains a director.
metadata.role: Co-founder & Director (former CEO of predecessor Surgical Design Studio)
metadata.priorBackground: Consultant colorectal surgeon (Auckland DHB); Associate Professor, University of Auckland; PhD in biomedical engineering; medical-device researcher.

nodes.name: Ian Bissett
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & Chief Medical Officer, The Insides Company

metadata.bio: Professor of Colorectal Surgery at the University of Auckland and adult lead of New Zealand's National Intestinal Failure Service; a clinical pioneer of nutrient (chyme) recycling.
metadata.priorBackground: Professor of Colorectal Surgery, University of Auckland; lead clinician, NZ National Intestinal Failure Service.

metadata.bio: Biomedical engineer (PhD) who co-founded the company and leads operations, bridging medical and engineering perspectives on the chyme reinfusion technology.
metadata.priorBackground: PhD in biomedical engineering; University of Auckland research background.

metadata.bio: Mechanical engineer who co-founded the company and leads technology development, holding several patents and design awards on the device.
metadata.priorBackground: Mechanical engineering; named inventor on company patents.

metadata.bio: James Sampson founded FileInvite in 2015 to solve the manual document-collection problem he faced at his Auckland web agency, Zyber, which he co-founded in 2009. He has led FileInvite as CEO since, growing it into a document-collection platform used across Australasia and the US.
metadata.priorBackground: Co-founder/director of Auckland web agency Zyber (founded 2009); studied architecture (degree completed) and launched his first company in his final year before a string of earlier ventures.

metadata.bio: An internationally known wedding photographer and one half of the photography duo Chasewild, having shot 280+ weddings across 13 countries. He founded Narrative to solve the time photographers spend culling images after a shoot and leads the company as CEO.
metadata.priorBackground: Wedding/portrait photographer; co-founder of photography duo Chasewild; speaker at photography conferences in Europe, the US and Australasia.

nodes.name: Steffan Levet
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder, Co-CEO & Co-Head of Engineering, Narrative

metadata.bio: Software engineer who co-founded Narrative with James Broadbent and co-leads the company and its engineering team, focusing on high-performance desktop apps that run machine learning locally on photographers' machines. He studied mechatronics before switching to computer science.
metadata.priorBackground: Software engineer; studied mechatronics then computer science; specific prior employers not confirmed.

metadata.bio: Former Otago Boys' High School mathematics teacher who founded LearnCoach in 2012 after a maths-explainer video he made for his students went viral. Won Young New Zealander of the Year in 2018.
metadata.priorBackground: Mathematics teacher at Otago Boys' High School; TeachNZ Future Maker (2016); Young New Zealander of the Year (2018).

metadata.bio: Co-founder and chief technology officer of LearnCoach and David Cameron's older brother. Holds a postgraduate engineering degree and previously worked as a developer at the academic peer-review platform Publons (acquired by a Thomson Reuters spinoff, Clarivate, in 2017).
metadata.priorBackground: Postgraduate engineering degree; developer at Publons (peer-review platform).

metadata.bio: Co-founded LearnCoach in 2012 with then-fiancee (later husband) David Cameron. A medical doctor with a Bachelor of Medical Sciences (Hons, bioethics), a Master of Entrepreneurship and a CFA charter; she was Miss World New Zealand 2015 and later moved into investment banking/finance.
metadata.priorBackground: Medical doctor (MBChB), Bachelor of Medical Science (Hons in bioethics), Master of Entrepreneurship, CFA Charterholder; Miss World New Zealand 2015; later worked in investment banking/finance.

metadata.bio: Co-founded Feed My Furbaby with his wife Amy in 2017 after repeatedly running out of food for their dog Jack and noticing how much plastic packaging he had used over the years. The light-bulb moment came leaving a supermarket with two large plastic bags of pet food.

Co-founded Feed My Furbaby in 2017 with her husband Ben to solve the recurring problem of running out of dog food for their dog Jack while reducing packaging waste. The business received backing from Icehouse Ventures' women-led ArcAngels II fund.
metadata.priorBackground: Per LinkedIn/ZoomInfo aggregator profiles, prior roles reportedly included Owner/Director at Furnished Rentals NZ and positions at Auckland Airport, Cato Bolam Consultants and Genesis Energy (not independently verified by a primary source).

metadata.bio: Australian co-founder and CEO of Datch. A former aircraft systems design engineer, he experienced first-hand how low-tech frontline processes limited industrial output and co-founded Datch to address it.
metadata.priorBackground: Aircraft systems design engineer at CAV Aerospace (2014-2017); earlier engineering work on submarines/aircraft; MSc in Aerospace Vehicle Design, Cranfield University; aerospace engineering alumnus of the University of Adelaide.

metadata.bio: New Zealand co-founder and Chief Product Officer of Datch. He leads product for the company's industrial frontline platform across manufacturing, energy and utilities.
metadata.priorBackground: Senior Project Engineer at Siemens (high-voltage / energy management); BE (Hons, First Class) in Electrical and Electronic Engineering, University of Canterbury.

metadata.bio: New Zealand co-founder and CTO of Datch. He leads engineering for the company's industrial voice and AI platform.
metadata.priorBackground: Engineering roles spanning the energy sector in New Zealand, the UK and Germany; electrical/electronic engineering background.

metadata.bio: Former All Black who became a prominent mental health advocate after speaking openly about his own depression; knighted for services to mental health. Co-founded Mentemia/Groov, drawing on his lived experience.
metadata.priorBackground: Former All Black rugby player and long-time mental health campaigner.

metadata.bio: Technology entrepreneur who co-founded Mentemia/Groov and served as its founding CEO. Previously co-founded and led mobile banking software company M-Com, which was acquired by Fiserv in 2011.
metadata.priorBackground: Co-founder and CEO of mobile banking software firm M-Com (acquired by Fiserv, 2011).

nodes.name: Symon Nausbaum
nodes.subtitle: Founder & CEO, Nectar (Nectar Money / Nectar NZ Limited)

metadata.bio: Finance-industry veteran who founded Nectar to build a fully digital consumer-lending platform in New Zealand; appointed a director of Nectar NZ Limited at its 2015 incorporation. Reported to have spent about 15 years as a director of Instant Finance Limited, a New Zealand subprime lender, before launching Nectar.
metadata.priorBackground: Director of Instant Finance Limited (~15 years); corporate finance roles including BDO Spicers (Manager, Corporate Finance); MBA, University of Auckland. (PwC/investment-banking experience appears in some secondary profiles but is not firmly sourced.)

metadata.bio: Founder and CEO of Melodics. Previously CEO of New Zealand DJ/music-software company Serato for about a decade before leaving in 2014, where he helped grow it into a global leader in DJ software. Conceived Melodics after observing that electronic musicians lacked an engaging way to practise pad/finger drumming.
metadata.priorBackground: Former CEO of Serato (DJ/music technology) for ~10 years; ~two decades across music and edtech.

nodes.name: Dr Eldon Tate
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & CEO (Founding CEO), Inhibit Coatings Limited

metadata.bio: Developed Inhibit Coatings' antimicrobial silver-nanoparticle technology during his PhD in chemistry at Victoria University of Wellington and co-founded the company in 2016, serving as founding CEO through multiple capital raises. Won the KiwiNet Norman Barry Foundation Breakthrough Innovator Award in 2020.
metadata.priorBackground: PhD in chemistry, Victoria University of Wellington (where the core technology was created), supervised by Prof Jim Johnston.

nodes.name: Professor Jim Johnston
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & Founding Director, Inhibit Coatings Limited

metadata.bio: Professor of chemistry at Victoria University of Wellington and co-inventor of the silver-binding antimicrobial coating technology; supervised Eldon Tate's PhD and is named as a founding director of Inhibit Coatings.
metadata.priorBackground: Professor of chemistry, Victoria University of Wellington; long-running research in functional nanomaterials.

nodes.name: Hayden Nicholson
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & Founding Director, Inhibit Coatings Limited

metadata.bio: Named as a founding director of Inhibit Coatings at its November 2016 founding, bringing coatings/polymer industry expertise from The Polymer Group, Auckland.
metadata.priorBackground: The Polymer Group, Auckland.

metadata.bio: Named as a co-founder of Inhibit Coatings at its November 2016 founding, as an industry colleague from The Polymer Group, Auckland.
metadata.priorBackground: The Polymer Group, Auckland.

metadata.bio: Named as a co-founder of Inhibit Coatings at its November 2016 founding, as an industry colleague from The Polymer Group, Auckland.
metadata.priorBackground: The Polymer Group, Auckland.

metadata.bio: Co-founded Rocos in 2017 and led it as CEO until its 2021 acquisition by DroneDeploy, where he became Head of Ground Robotics. Previously was CTO and part of the founding team at NZX-listed mobile marketing firm Plexure (formerly VMob).
metadata.priorBackground: Plexure (CTO / founding team); Master's in International Business, University of Auckland

metadata.bio: Co-founded Rocos in 2017 and served as CTO until the 2021 DroneDeploy acquisition, after which he became Head of Engineering, Ground Robotics at DroneDeploy. Previously was Head of Engineering at Plexure and held architecture/development roles at Endava.
metadata.priorBackground: Head of Engineering at Plexure (ex-VMob); Group Head of Development / Lead Architect at Endava; LLB and BCom (Finance), University of Otago

nodes.name: Mike Carden
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder (formerly Co-CEO; now Chief Revenue Officer), Joyous

metadata.bio: Serial New Zealand SaaS entrepreneur and co-founder of Joyous. He moved into the Chief Revenue Officer role in 2024 when the company ended its shared 'Collective CEO' model, while remaining an executive director on the board.
metadata.role: Co-founder (formerly Co-CEO; now Chief Revenue Officer)
metadata.priorBackground: Held senior roles at HP New Zealand before founding HR SaaS company Sonar6, acquired by Cornerstone OnDemand (NASDAQ: CSOD) for US$14m in 2012, where he then served as VP Small Business Operations. Also chaired AskNicely and Promapp (acquired by Nintex).

nodes.name: Philip Carden
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder (formerly Co-CEO; now Executive Director of Strategic Accounts), Joyous

metadata.bio: Co-founder of Joyous alongside his brother Mike, originally leading technology development. He transitioned to Executive Director of Strategic Accounts in 2024 and remains an executive director on the board.
metadata.role: Co-founder (formerly Co-CEO; now Executive Director of Strategic Accounts)
metadata.priorBackground: Spent about a decade at Alcatel-Lucent, becoming a senior vice-president and global head of its consulting services division (which included Bell Labs), based in Paris before returning to New Zealand. Holds a Bachelor of Commerce from the University of Auckland.

nodes.name: Ruby Kolesky
nodes.subtitle: Chief Executive Officer (joined 2020; Co-CEO/Chief Product Officer; appointed sole CEO 31 May 2024), Joyous

metadata.bio: Product leader who joined Joyous in 2020 and was part of its 'Collective CEO' triumvirate, leading product as Chief Product Officer, before being appointed sole Chief Executive Officer on 31 May 2024. She is an executive leader but not a founding co-owner of the 2017 company.
metadata.role: Chief Executive Officer (joined 2020; Co-CEO/Chief Product Officer; appointed sole CEO 31 May 2024)
metadata.priorBackground: Held leadership positions at New Zealand SaaS companies Vista Group and AskNicely before joining Joyous.

metadata.bio: Founded Dexibit after seeing a museum guard manually counting visitors with a clicker. She led the company as CEO and director through to its 2026 acquisition by accesso and was its largest shareholder (~25%).
metadata.priorBackground: Around a decade in technology transformation and network analytics at Hewlett Packard, Israeli software company Amdocs, and Finco.

metadata.bio: Co-founder and Chief Operating Officer and director, responsible for Dexibit's global business operations. He is married to CEO Angie Judge.

Co-founder and commercial lead of Avertana (VP Commercial / Commercial Director). Previously worked at New Zealand biotech LanzaTech alongside his Avertana co-founders, where the idea for the slag-refining technology originated. University of Auckland BSc.
metadata.priorBackground: LanzaTech (New Zealand biotech); Redoubt Advisory; University of Auckland (BSc)

metadata.bio: Co-founder of Avertana who served as CEO from the company's early days until around 2020, then became Founding Director. He led development of the proprietary process and the demonstration plant. A University of Auckland engineering graduate and ex-LanzaTech (worked on the New Zealand Steel site); recognised in the University of Auckland 40 Under 40.
metadata.priorBackground: LanzaTech; Greenlane Biogas; University of Auckland (engineering)

metadata.bio: Co-founder of Avertana, credited in company accounts with pointing out that the steelmaking slag was rich in titanium, sparking the concept behind Avertana's extraction technology. Came from LanzaTech with the other co-founders.
metadata.priorBackground: LanzaTech (New Zealand biotech)

nodes.name: Chris Oze
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & Chief Science Officer, Aspiring Materials

metadata.bio: Geologist who developed the underlying science showing how olivine-rich ultramafic rock can mineralise CO2, work originating in research (with Allan Scott) on materials that could be produced on Mars. A Breakthrough Energy Fellow and the company's Chief Science Officer.
metadata.priorBackground: Geology professor / academic researcher; reported in 2021 as US-based; co-developed the core process with University of Canterbury collaborators.

nodes.name: Mark Chadderton
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & Chief Executive Officer, Aspiring Materials

metadata.bio: CEO of Aspiring Materials and a Breakthrough Energy Fellow. He volunteered with the company before committing full-time in early 2022 and now leads its scale-up and commercialisation.
metadata.priorBackground: Process/operations engineer with global oil, gas and dairy experience at Chevron (Wheatstone LNG), Santos, British Sugar and Fonterra. MBA (Heriot-Watt University); BE Chemical & Process Engineering (University of Canterbury); PG Dip in Dairy Science and Technology.

metadata.bio: Anne Fulton is the founder and CEO of Fuel50, an AI-powered talent marketplace and skills platform. A long-time organizational psychologist and executive career coach (around two decades in the field), she is the author of 'The Career Engagement Game' and 'The Talent Revolution', and has grown Fuel50 into a global HR-tech company.
metadata.priorBackground: Roughly 20 years as an organizational psychologist, executive career coach, and corporate employment strategist; author of two books on career engagement and talent; led other ventures before Fuel50 (specific prior company names not confirmed from authoritative sources).

nodes.name: Jo Mills
nodes.subtitle: Co-Founder & President (formerly Chief Experience Officer), Fuel50

metadata.bio: Jo Mills co-founded Fuel50 and served as Chief Experience Officer, overseeing client success and product/consulting offerings, before being promoted to President in October 2023. Based in Auckland, she has a background in organizational psychology and the NZ startup ecosystem.
metadata.priorBackground: Bachelor of Social Science (Massey University) and Graduate Certificate of Career Development (Auckland University of Technology); active in the NZ startup ecosystem including the Angel Association New Zealand and as a startup mentor at Ministry of Awesome.

metadata.bio: Wellington-based industrial designer who developed Foundry Lab's microwave-based Digital Metal Casting technology, initially as a backyard project before founding the company in 2018. Leads the company as CEO.
metadata.priorBackground: Industrial designer (~15 years' experience); Bachelor of Design at Victoria University of Wellington (2000-2004); previously worked at design firm Designbrand (Island Bay) and founded his own studio Makegood in Lower Hutt before starting Foundry Lab.

metadata.bio: World-leading plant UV photobiologist with more than 15 years of research in the field. He founded BioLumic in 2013 to commercialise his Massey University photobiology research into UV light treatments that activate beneficial, non-GMO crop traits.
metadata.priorBackground: Took up a faculty position at Massey University, New Zealand, in 2010, becoming Professor in Plant Photobiology and Entrepreneur-in-Residence; opened a Massey-hosted UV photobiology R&D facility.

metadata.bio: Co-founder of Jasper and now its sole CEO. He returned to New Zealand in 2019 after roughly a decade in London's property and finance industry managing multi-billion-dollar portfolios across Asia-Pacific and Europe, including a role at M7 Real Estate. He was named in the University of Auckland's 40 Under 40 (Business Leaders) and holds a Bachelor of Property from the University of Auckland.
metadata.priorBackground: Investment/role at M7 Real Estate in London; ~decade in London property and finance managing multi-billion-dollar Asia-Pacific and European portfolios. Bachelor of Property, University of Auckland.

nodes.name: Mark Hurley
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & former Co-CEO (left in 2023 to lead spinout Caruso), Jasper

metadata.bio: Serial entrepreneur and co-founder of Jasper, where he served as Co-CEO. He founded the New Zealand digital product agency Little Giant in 2014 (acquired by Dentsu Aegis Network in 2017, becoming part of Isobar) and was a 2017 EY Entrepreneur of the Year finalist. In 2023 he moved across to co-found and lead Caruso, the SaaS company spun out of Jasper.
metadata.role: Co-founder & former Co-CEO (left in 2023 to lead spinout Caruso)
metadata.priorBackground: Founder/CEO of Little Giant (sold to Dentsu Aegis Network, 2017); EY Entrepreneur of the Year finalist 2017.

nodes.name: Oliver Shaw
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & CTO (left in 2023 to lead spinout Caruso), Jasper

metadata.bio: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer of Jasper, leading its technology and platform build. Before Jasper he was a partner and senior developer at Little Giant (which was acquired by Dentsu and integrated into Isobar). When Jasper spun its software out as Caruso in 2023, he moved across to co-found and co-lead Caruso as Co-CEO/CTO.
metadata.role: Co-founder & CTO (left in 2023 to lead spinout Caruso)
metadata.priorBackground: Partner and senior developer at Little Giant (acquired by Dentsu/Isobar) before co-founding Jasper. Studied at the University of Auckland.

metadata.bio: New Zealand environmentalist and entrepreneur who founded Ethique (originally 'Sorbet') in Christchurch in 2012 as the world's first zero-waste beauty brand. Named a Foreign Policy 'Global Thinker' (2016) and EY Young Entrepreneur of the Year (2019). She stepped down as Ethique CEO in April 2023, remaining as founder and board member, and later launched plastic-free drinks brand Incrediballs.
metadata.priorBackground: Studied a Bachelor of Science at the University of Canterbury, where she began developing the solid-bar products as a student. Later founded the drinks brand Incrediballs and the values-led investment/mentoring firm Nous (~NZ$12.3M).

metadata.bio: Economist, environmentalist and social entrepreneur who founded Conscious Consumers (which became Cogo) and leads the company as CEO. He started the venture after working as an economist at the New Zealand Treasury focused on climate change policy.
metadata.priorBackground: Economist at the New Zealand Treasury (climate change policy); graduate of Victoria University of Wellington; co-founded the 'Conscious Consumers' venture that rebranded to Cogo.

nodes.name: Melissa Keys
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder, Conscious Consumers (predecessor to Cogo), Cogo

metadata.bio: Co-founded Conscious Consumers with Ben Gleisner in Wellington around 2009, helping grow it from a voluntary charity into a social enterprise and developing its business-accreditation framework. She is reported to have departed around the 2016 restructure when the company rebranded to Cogo.
metadata.priorBackground: Co-founder and sustainability lead of Conscious Consumers; later reported in a sustainability/environment management role at Citycare Property.

metadata.bio: Co-founder and CEO of McCarthyFinch; previously Chief Digital Officer at MinterEllisonRuddWatts, where the venture originated. Named IDC DX Leader of the Year (2019) for legal-industry innovation. After the Onit acquisition he became general manager of the Onit AI Center of Excellence.
metadata.priorBackground: Chief Digital Officer at MinterEllisonRuddWatts; 15+ years in digital innovation and AI in the legal industry across Australasia.

metadata.bio: Veteran New Zealand technology executive turned founder; CEO and director of Organic Initiative since 2015. An Officer of the NZ Order of Merit (ONZM, 2018) for services to technology and business; she is a breast cancer survivor.
metadata.priorBackground: Former CEO of Microsoft New Zealand (left 2007) and a Pivotal executive in Australasia; founding CEO of the TZ1 Registry, an environmental/carbon-asset registry acquired by London's Markit Group in 2009, where she became Global Managing Director, Environmental Markets. Board roles include Network for Learning (N4L) and others.

metadata.bio: Co-founder/creator of Organic Initiative; a health expert, herbalist and nutritionist focused on healthy, sustainable products. Later founded eco nappy brand Noopii.
metadata.priorBackground: Background as a herbalist and nutritionist; subsequently founder/creator of Noopii (eco-friendly nappies, launched into NZ supermarkets in late 2019).

nodes.name: Iain Hosie
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & Director (former managing director/CEO; Technical Director/CTO), Nanolayr

metadata.bio: Scientist involved in nanofibre production, development and innovation since 2008; co-founded the company in 2009 and led it as managing director from a startup to a globally recognised nanofibre manufacturer.
metadata.role: Co-founder & Director (former managing director/CEO; Technical Director/CTO)
metadata.priorBackground: BSc in Biochemistry; background spanning environmental health, government policy, product development and sales; previously worked in the air-filtration industry.

metadata.bio: Engineer who co-founded Revolution Fibres (now Nanolayr) in 2009 while working in the air-filtration industry, seeking to develop a high-performance nanofibre air filter.
metadata.priorBackground: Engineering background; previously worked in the air-filtration industry.

metadata.bio: Entrepreneur and founder of New Zealand ventilation company HRV who co-founded Revolution Fibres (now Nanolayr) in 2009; HRV was the company's first customer for its nanofibre air filters.
metadata.priorBackground: Entrepreneur; founder of HRV (Home Ventilation), a New Zealand ventilation-systems company.

metadata.bio: Christchurch-born hospitality entrepreneur who, with her sister, bought and ran The Spire, a boutique hotel in Queenstown, before selling it in 2014. Frustrated by existing hotel admin tools, she co-founded Preno to simplify and automate accommodation management. She studied IT at a New Zealand polytechnic.
metadata.priorBackground: Owner/operator of The Spire boutique hotel, Queenstown (bought with her sister; sold 2014); studied information technology at a New Zealand polytechnic.

metadata.bio: Software developer and co-founder who leads Preno's product and technology, overseeing design, development, deployment and monitoring. He met Amelia Gain while studying IT at a New Zealand polytechnic and went into software development before building Preno together.
metadata.priorBackground: Software development background; studied IT alongside Amelia Gain at a New Zealand polytechnic. Sometimes listed by full name Maksym Podolian.

metadata.bio: Founder of NILO (established 2018) and its Managing Director / board member. A former molecular biologist (first-class honours, University of Canterbury) who spent 17 years in Japan, where he and his business partner were the first foreigners to IPO two e-commerce companies on the Japan Stock Exchange before returning to NZ to invest in deep tech.
metadata.priorBackground: Molecular biology (University of Canterbury); 17 years in Japan founding and listing e-commerce firms (incl. ValueCommerce); serial NZ startup investor and co-founder of construction-tech firm Utecture.

metadata.bio: Founder and CEO of Parrot Analytics, leading the company in global audience demand measurement since its founding. Recognized as a Variety 30 Under 30 Hollywood leader, a Forbes 40 Under 40, and a University of Auckland 40 Under 40 alumnus.
metadata.priorBackground: University of Auckland: Bachelor of Biomedical Science (neurobiology, 2009) and Master of Bioscience Enterprise; background in neuroscience. Drew on the University of Auckland entrepreneurship ecosystem (Velocity, Chiasma, The ICEHOUSE, Ice Angels) to launch the company.

metadata.bio: Founder and former CEO of marketing/personalization platform Sailthru (started 2008, acquired 2018); leads Solve as CEO. Based in New York.
metadata.priorBackground: Founder & CEO of Sailthru (2008-2016+); also a partner/advisor at Bowery Capital.

metadata.bio: New Zealand-born tech entrepreneur who co-founded Polar Bear Farm (early iPhone app company, 2007) and Carnival Labs / Carnival.io (mobile marketing automation, acquired by Sailthru in 2016), then co-founded Solve. Based between New Zealand and New York.
metadata.priorBackground: Co-founder of Carnival.io (acquired by Sailthru, 2016) and Polar Bear Farm; later worked at Sailthru.

metadata.bio: Co-founder of Solve who leads product out of Portland, Oregon; came from the Sailthru team. His role is corroborated by Movac's investment note.
metadata.priorBackground: Part of the Sailthru team prior to co-founding Solve.

metadata.bio: Supply-chain technology entrepreneur who led TNX as founder and CEO. He previously founded transport-optimisation software firm Clear Abacus (acquired by GT Nexus in 2013) and has worked across supply chain and technology internationally. After the Transporeon acquisition he held senior product roles at Transporeon and later at Trimble Transportation.
metadata.priorBackground: Founder of Clear Abacus (acquired by GT Nexus, 2013); broad international supply-chain/technology career; post-acquisition product leadership at Transporeon / Trimble.

metadata.bio: Co-founder and Managing Director of TNX, focused on supply chain and machine learning, associated with the company's Berlin operations. In interviews he discussed using machine learning to model carrier behaviour and pricing in freight procurement.
metadata.priorBackground: Background combining supply chain, machine learning and financial-markets expertise; led TNX's Berlin-based operations.

metadata.bio: Co-founder and Managing Director of TNX Logistics who contributed software-engineering and product expertise. He is reported to have later worked as a software engineer (associated with Globus).
metadata.priorBackground: Software-engineering background; co-founded TNX; subsequently reported as a software engineer.

nodes.name: Ehsan Vaghefi
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & CEO, Toku (formerly Toku Eyes / Toku, Inc.)
nodes.location: Auckland, New Zealand / San Diego, USA

metadata.bio: Bioengineer and Associate Professor of medical imaging/AI in optometry and ophthalmology at the University of Auckland. He conceived the THEIA technology during his biomedical-engineering PhD; his father's blindness from undiagnosed congenital glaucoma motivated his focus on preventable blindness.
metadata.priorBackground: PhD in biomedical engineering / ophthalmic imaging, University of Auckland; Associate Professor / senior research fellow at the University of Auckland.

nodes.name: David Squirrell
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & Chief Medical Officer, Toku (formerly Toku Eyes / Toku, Inc.)

metadata.bio: Consultant ophthalmologist and University of Auckland academic who led/chaired New Zealand's northern-region diabetic eye screening programme, the clinical problem that inspired Toku's THEIA tool. Independently confirmed as co-founder and former CMO, though he no longer appears on the company's current team page.
metadata.priorBackground: Consultant ophthalmologist; chair of the northern-region diabetic retinopathy screening programme; academic, University of Auckland.

metadata.bio: Mechanical engineer with 30+ years of commercial experience and a Masters in Mechanical Engineering (First Class Honours) who has undertaken PhD research into atmospheric buoyancy vortices. He conceived the idea after watching a long-lived dust devil form on an airfield in Matamata, New Zealand in 2014.
metadata.priorBackground: Masters in Mechanical Engineering (University of Auckland); over 30 years of commercial engineering experience; background in induction heating and related systems.

nodes.name: Richard Flay
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder & Chief Scientific Officer, Vortex Power Systems

metadata.bio: Professor of Mechanical Engineering at the University of Auckland (Professor Emeritus from 2024) and Director of its Yacht Research Unit. An expert in aerodynamics, fluid mechanics, thermodynamics and wind engineering; he designed the world's first wind tunnel capable of producing twisted flow for testing yacht sails. He co-developed the vortex technology with Neil Hawkes.
metadata.priorBackground: Professor / Professor Emeritus of Mechanical Engineering, University of Auckland; Director of the Yacht Research Unit; long research career in wind engineering, aerodynamics and yacht/sail testing.

metadata.bio: Owner of iconic NZ soft drink brand Foxton Fizz. He started Upstock as a side project to solve his own frustrations fielding disorganised wholesale orders, then recruited Philip Fierlinger to build it into a company while continuing to run Foxton Fizz.
metadata.priorBackground: Founder/owner of Foxton Fizz (soft drink brand)

metadata.bio: Co-founder and original product designer of accounting software company Xero, with 30+ years in technology. He was brought in by Matt Watson to build Upstock and serves as co-CEO leading its growth and Australian expansion.
metadata.priorBackground: Co-founder and designer of Xero

metadata.bio: Former Chief Product Officer at Xero with 25+ years in technology. He co-founded Upstock with Philip Fierlinger, with whom he worked closely at Xero, and serves as co-CEO.
metadata.priorBackground: Chief Product Officer at Xero

nodes.name: Milot Zeqiri
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder, Group CEO & Executive Director, ArchiPro

metadata.bio: Co-founder and Group CEO of ArchiPro, which he started with his wife Brittany Gribben in their bedroom in March 2014. He arrived in New Zealand in 1999 as a 17-year-old refugee from the Kosovo war and later earned a Bachelor of Design at Auckland University of Technology (AUT).
metadata.priorBackground: Background in selling products to specifiers, builders and homeowners; Bachelor of Design, AUT; arrived in NZ as a refugee from Kosovo in 1999.

metadata.bio: Co-founder and COO of ArchiPro, which she launched with her husband Milot Zeqiri in March 2014. She runs the company's operations; she is a major shareholder (reported ~49.8% of ArchiPro Limited as of late 2024).
metadata.priorBackground: Background in selling products to specifiers, builders and homeowners; personal experience with building and renovating homes.

metadata.bio: Founder and CEO of Pyper Vision, leading its fog-casting and earlier fog-dispersal technology for aviation. She learned to fly young on her family farm and comes from a line of aviators; she started her first business in high school, with the Pyper Vision idea emerging via the Young Enterprise Scheme. Named Kiwibank New Zealand Innovator of the Year (2023).
metadata.priorBackground: From Canterbury, New Zealand. Built an earlier business (Flatpak, quad-bike toolboxes) as a teenager via the Young Enterprise Scheme; left university after a few months to focus on the company.

metadata.bio: CTO of Pyper Vision. He joined through his final-year engineering project at the University of Canterbury working with Emily Blythe, then continued via a research Master's before becoming full-time. His work spans scaling the product from lab to airport, product development, and operations. He is the CTO, not a founder.
metadata.priorBackground: Engineering graduate of the University of Canterbury; participated in accelerator/development programmes including Venture Up, Te Ohaka and Startmate.

metadata.bio: Founded HeartLab in 2018 at age 18 while a University of Auckland student studying applied mathematics and statistics and working as a researcher at the Auckland Bioengineering Institute. He leads HeartLab as CEO and had earlier founded a robotics education company in high school.
metadata.priorBackground: University of Auckland (applied mathematics and statistics); undergraduate researcher at the Auckland Bioengineering Institute; founded a robotics education company in high school.

metadata.bio: Cardiologist and cardiac imaging specialist whose explanation of the slow, error-prone nature of manual scan review inspired the company. He is a specialist in general cardiology and internal medicine and has practised as a cardiologist in Auckland (North Shore Hospital).
metadata.priorBackground: Cardiologist specialising in general cardiology and internal medicine; cardiologist at North Shore Hospital (Auckland).

metadata.bio: New Zealand entrepreneur with 20+ years in digital marketing. He founded Shuttlerock in 2011 in Nelson, starting with a small team from his kitchen table, and built it into a global Creative-as-a-Service business. Named EY Entrepreneur of the Year New Zealand 2024.
metadata.priorBackground: Earlier founded and listed ValueClick Japan on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in May 2000, reported as the first foreigner to list a company on that exchange. Holds a Bachelor of Economics from Keio University.

metadata.bio: Co-founded Astrix Astronautics in January 2021 as its founding CEO (holding ~49%) while a University of Auckland physics student, having paused her degree to pursue the venture. She secured early backing from Rocket Lab founder Peter Beck and later departed the company.
metadata.priorBackground: Studied physics at the University of Auckland (paused her degree after about 2.5 years to start Astrix). Was around 21 at founding. Has since gone by the name Fia Arshavskaya.

metadata.bio: Co-founded Astrix Astronautics in 2021, originally joining as a research and development engineer (~14% stake), and now serves as CEO. He met co-founder Will Hunter through the Auckland Programme for Space Systems student satellite competition.
metadata.priorBackground: Studied physics at the University of Auckland.

metadata.bio: Co-founded Astrix Astronautics in 2021 and serves as Chief Technology Officer (~37% stake at founding), leading development of the company's inflatable solar array and deployment technology. He met his co-founders via the Auckland Programme for Space Systems.
metadata.priorBackground: Studied mechanical engineering at the University of Auckland.

nodes.name: Brendon Petrich
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder (founding CEO; no longer CEO), vWork (vWorkApp)

metadata.bio: Co-founder and founding CEO of vWork/vWorkApp, based in Auckland. NZ Herald reporting from the company's early years describes VisFleet/vWorkApp as 'led by Brendon Petrich'. He is no longer the current CEO.
metadata.priorBackground: Reported MBA, University of Auckland; prior commercial/leadership roles cited at SMX, Air New Zealand and Television New Zealand (not independently verified).

metadata.bio: Co-founder of vWorkApp who led technology and helped establish the company's San Francisco presence; vWorkApp spun out of parent company VisFleet, where he was CTO. A New Zealander who went on to senior machine-learning/AI roles, including Director of Machine Learning at Netflix and later OpenAI.
metadata.priorBackground: M.Sc Computer Science and BMus, University of Auckland; previously CTO at VisFleet, Product Manager at iVistra Technology and Tech Manager at Datacom; later Netflix (Director of ML) and OpenAI.

metadata.bio: Award-winning researcher and AI entrepreneur with 25+ years in insights; twice named to the ESOMAR Insights250. She founded Yabble in 2017 and led it through its 2024 acquisition by YouGov.
metadata.priorBackground: 25+ years in research and insights across agency and client side; BSc in Geography, University of Canterbury (1998).

metadata.bio: Co-founder of Yabble heading revenue and operations, with 20+ years in operations, marketing and brand management. She co-founded the company with Kathryn Topp in 2017.
metadata.priorBackground: 20+ years in operations, marketing and brand management, including roles associated with Diageo Wines and Treasury Wine Estates.

metadata.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Zincovery/Zethos, which he started while a master's student in chemical and process engineering at the University of Canterbury. He won Callaghan Innovation's C-Prize (2019/20) for the zinc-recycling technology and the KiwiNet Breakthrough Innovator Award (2022).
metadata.priorBackground: Studied chemical and process engineering (BE(Hons), ME) at the University of Canterbury.

nodes.name: Aaron Marshall
nodes.subtitle: Co-founder; Tech & Innovation Lead, Zethos (formerly Zincovery)

metadata.bio: Professor of chemical and process engineering at the University of Canterbury and an electrochemist who developed the process behind Zincovery for recovering zinc from steel-industry waste. He supervised co-founder Jonathan Ring's master's research that led to the spin-out.
metadata.priorBackground: Joined the University of Canterbury Faculty of Engineering in 2009; appointed full professor in December 2021. Earlier studies at Massey University and a PhD from the Norwegian University of Science and Technology.

metadata.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Spoke (Spoke Phone), a serial NZ tech entrepreneur. He patented original protocols for text (TXT) messaging early in his career and previously founded recruitment-software company Findly (later part of Symphony Talent).
metadata.priorBackground: Founder of Findly (acquired by Symphony Talent); patented early TXT/SMS messaging protocols; described as a multi-time founder with prior exits (e.g. QuietAgent, StaffCV).

metadata.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Spoke (Spoke Phone), responsible for the company's engineering and technology. He previously built a large-scale call-centre stack reportedly supporting around 30,000 concurrent calls/agents and worked with Jason Kerr at a prior company before they began developing Spoke in late 2015.
metadata.priorBackground: Senior Vice President of Engineering at Findly (Symphony Talent) and LiveOps; built a call-centre stack reportedly supporting ~30,000 concurrent calls/agents.

metadata.bio: Maritime professional who built SeaLogs to solve compliance and operations problems she faced at sea, including losing a paper logbook holding nearly six months of records days before an audit. Also works as a maritime consultant.
metadata.priorBackground: States over 16 years working at sea on a range of vessels worldwide; skipper at Explore Group; ran maritime operations that grew from single-vessel start-ups to multi-vessel fleets, which she says led to two multi-million-dollar exits.

metadata.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Relab, which he started in 2016 with Leon Hong after three years of evening/weekend development. A migrant to New Zealand, he leads the company's strategy and growth.
metadata.priorBackground: Reported ~15 years at large NZ corporates including Air New Zealand and Spark; also worked with the Brave New Coin startup.

metadata.bio: Co-founder of Relab (started in 2016 with Knight Hou) and its technical lead. Grew up in South Africa before migrating to New Zealand. His public title varies between CTO and CFO across sources.
metadata.priorBackground: Application developer/support analyst at Auckland Council (2012-2015, including Auckland Unitary Plan work); also worked on the Booktrack startup.

nodes.name: Jimmy Wu (James Wu)
nodes.subtitle: Founder & Executive Director / CEO, Zappy (Zappy Limited)

metadata.bio: Founder of the company, launched in 2012 as Payport (later Parcelport, then Zappy). A serial entrepreneur born in China who grew up near Auckland, he started his first ventures as a teenager and ran a domain-name and email hosting business during university before building the logistics company in Auckland.
metadata.priorBackground: University degree in statistics; earlier founded a domain-name and email hosting company that grew to ~30,000 users; serial entrepreneur from a young age.

metadata.bio: Fintech founder who launched payments platform Payleadr in 2019; that experience surfaced the beauty industry's need for membership solutions, leading him to start aglow in 2023. He serves as aglow's CEO.
metadata.priorBackground: Founder/Managing Director of Payleadr (from 2018/2019); connected to Tyro Payments; based in Sydney.

metadata.bio: Beauty-tech and SaaS executive with 15+ years building software for the beauty and wellness industry. She co-founded aglow and leads revenue as CRO.
metadata.priorBackground: Senior roles at Timely, Xero and Kitomba (per company about page); media also cite CarbonCrop. NZ-rooted SaaS career.

metadata.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Onside. Previously Innovation Manager at Synlait Farms, where the idea for Onside originated. Holds a PhD from Cornell University.
metadata.priorBackground: Innovation Manager at Synlait Farms; PhD, Cornell University

metadata.bio: Co-founder of Onside. Previously co-founded Synlait and headed Synlait Farms, where the Onside idea took shape; she continued on the Onside board.
metadata.priorBackground: Co-founder of Synlait; led Synlait Farms

metadata.bio: Co-founder of Onside with an investment banking background (12 years at Credit Suisse in New York and New Zealand). Has also chaired Orion Health.
metadata.priorBackground: Investment banking (Credit Suisse); chair of Orion Health

metadata.bio: Co-founded the company (as MenuAid) in 2021 with his wife Elise after experiencing dinner decision fatigue, funding it by selling his stake in his prior venture Mutu. Leads Appetise as CEO and is the public face of its fundraising and B2B insights pivot.
metadata.priorBackground: Previously founder/CEO of Mutu, a New Zealand peer-to-peer asset/rental marketplace. Formerly went by the surname Skilton (hence LinkedIn handle 'tobyskilton').

metadata.bio: Co-founded MenuAid/Appetise in 2021 with husband Toby. A trained nutritionist, she brought food and nutrition subject-matter expertise to the meal-planning product and serves as Chief Operating Officer.
metadata.priorBackground: Trained nutritionist.

metadata.bio: Founder and CEO of OnSend and of Hitrak, the freight-management SaaS that spun out of OnSend's internal technology. A former mountain guide who climbed Mount Everest before moving into logistics.
metadata.priorBackground: Ex-Mainfreight (joined its graduate programme and managed one of New Zealand's busiest branches); earlier career as a mountain guide who climbed Mount Everest. Also founder & CEO of Hitrak.

metadata.bio: Mechanical engineer who founded Mushroom Material in 2020, inspired by the plastic and polystyrene pollution he saw on a 2018 surfing trip to Indonesia. He leads the company's product, materials and commercial strategy.
metadata.priorBackground: Born in South Africa, raised in Dubai, educated in New Zealand. Bachelor of Engineering (Mechanical) from the University of Auckland (2009-2014), specializing in composite materials. Designed plastic injection-moulding equipment at Fisher & Paykel Appliances, was part of the founding team at CIE spin-out StretchSense, and joined Entrepreneur First as a Founder in Residence.

metadata.bio: Mechatronics engineer with over a decade of experience in automation and scaling manufacturing. Co-founded Mushroom Material in 2020 and leads operations and the production process; also described as CTO.
metadata.priorBackground: Bachelor of Engineering (Mechatronics, Robotics & Automation) from the University of Auckland. Previously a QA/QC engineer at StretchSense and a field engineer at Greefa Australasia.

metadata.bio: Dutch-born business actuary and financial modeler with over a decade working with major insurance brands across Europe and Asia. He started Montoux out of frustration with outdated actuarial tools and led the company as Co-CEO.
metadata.priorBackground: Career actuary in life insurance (~15 years) across Europe and Asia before founding Montoux; later associated with Opio.

metadata.bio: Dutch expat software engineer and technical leader who built the early prototypes that became Montoux's platform and led the company's engineering team. Described in company sources as CTO & Co-Founder (self-styled on LinkedIn as Software Engineer & Technical Leader).
metadata.priorBackground: Software engineer and technical leader; co-founded Montoux in Wellington (Victoria University of Wellington connections) after developing the initial product prototypes around 2010-2011.

metadata.bio: Dutch expat user-interaction designer and the third of the three Dutch surfing co-founders who came together in Lyall Bay, Wellington. Multiple press sources describe him as Montoux's Co-Founder, Chief Operations Officer and Creative Director.
metadata.priorBackground: User-interaction / UX designer; co-founded Montoux in Wellington in 2012 with Klaas Stijnen and Gert Verhoog.

metadata.bio: Bacon was pursuing a PhD in sports science (injury prediction/prevention through data) at the University of Canterbury when he co-founded Komodo in 2018. He leads the company as CEO.
metadata.priorBackground: PhD candidate in sports science at the University of Canterbury, researching injury prevention via data.

metadata.bio: Wood was studying law and commerce at the University of Canterbury when he co-founded Komodo in 2018. He leads product as Chief Product Officer and is based in Christchurch.
metadata.priorBackground: Law and commerce student at the University of Canterbury.

metadata.bio: Goodson was finishing a software engineering degree at the University of Canterbury when he co-founded Komodo in 2018, serving as CTO. He has since moved to automotive-parts startup Partly, where public profiles list him as Director of Engineering; his current Komodo involvement is unclear and 2025 funding coverage named only Bacon and Wood.
metadata.priorBackground: Software engineering student at the University of Canterbury; later Director of Engineering at Partly.

metadata.bio: New Zealand-raised software developer who created Landlord Studio while living in London, after buying a rental property and finding existing management tools inadequate. He grew the app from a side project into a venture-backed company and leads it as CEO.
